articleTitle: Unveiling Valuable Insights: Leveraging Apriori Algorithm for Association Rule Mining and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the era of big data, it is particularly important to use big data technology to extract valuable information from large datasets, and the significance of data mining lies in exploring the hidden knowledge within the data. This paper focuses on data mining on movie datasets and uses association rule techniques to extract correlation relationships among valuable data items from the dataset. The Apriori algorithm is a classic algorithm for association rules, which identifies frequent item sets to generate strong association rules and ultimately reveal the relationships between different datasets. Through the validation using datasets and the implementation of the Apriori algorithm in Python, this paper demonstrates the effectiveness of revealing the strongest association relationships within the data. By discovering association rules within the dataset, it helps us understand the hidden patterns and correlations behind the data, providing references and support for decision-making and predictions. On the basis of the prior algorithm of association rules, the data correlation analysis shows that users can recommend movies more accurately according to the strong correlation relationship between movie types, thus providing reference significance for various practical applications based on association rules.

articleTitle: RGB-D Point Cloud Correction using Information of Adjacent Frames
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Breathing motion compensation is an important issue to be addressed in robotic thoracic and abdominal surgery. In recent years, with the widespread application of RGB-D depth cameras based on TOF imaging principles, respiratory monitoring has become a trend. However, due to the multi-path interference of TOF principle RGB-D cameras, various measures are often taken to avoid interference when using multiple cameras for respiratory monitoring. In this paper, a deep learning network that fuses previous frame information is proposed for respiratory motion point clouds under multi-path interference. At the same time, a method for generating multi-path interference regions from clean point clouds is designed, and a dataset is created for training. Our experiments prove that point cloud misalignment caused by multi-path interference can be effectively corrected using a neural network that fuses information from previous frame point clouds.

articleTitle: Scenic buildings Recognition Based on MobileNetV1 Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The recognition of images in natural scenes based on mobile devices has become mainstream. The cost of recognizing images through mobile phone photography is low and the operation is simple. A method based on MobileNetV1 and transfer learning is proposed to identify scenic buildings in China due to the small sample size and low recognition accuracy. Firstly, collect a dataset of buildings from famous scenic spots in China, and use methods such as flipping, flipping, scaling, brightness adjustment, adding noise, and pixel translation to improve the diversity of the data samples and avoid overfitting the model. Use MobileNetV1 to pre train the model on the ImageNet dataset; Then, based on the pre trained results, a MobileNetV1 network for scenic spot building recognition was constructed. The weights of the pre trained MobileNetV1 network model were transferred to the constructed MobileNetV1 network for model weight initialization, thereby reducing training costs. The outcomes of the experiment demonstrate that using transfer learning enables the model to complete training quickly, and the accuracy is greatly improved compared to non-transfer learning methods. Research has shown that using methods based on MobileNetV1 and transfer learning effectively solves the problems of small sample size and low accuracy in scenic building recognition, providing a new method for scenic building recognition.

articleTitle: Cross-Modality Pedestrian Re-Identification via Modality Data Homogenization and Cross-layer Feature Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Visible-Infrared Cross-Modality pedestrian Re-identification (CmRe-id) seeks to identify pedestrian photos captured by multiple cameras that show the same pedestrian. However, the challenge of cross-modality feature mismatch caused by data heterogeneity remains. To address this challenge, we propose Modality Data Homogenization and Cross-layer Feature Aggregation Network(MHFA) in this paper. For improved modality alignment, we introduce RGB Modality Data Homogenization (MDH) using grayscale conversion. To enhance feature representations, we develop Cross-Layer Feature Aggregation (CLFA). The findings obtained from our extensive evaluation clearly establish the superiority of our suggested technique over current approaches, effectively addressing the limitations of cross-modality pedestrian re-identification.

articleTitle: Initialization with Description Information and Incorporating Structure Learning for Efficient Dynamic Knowledge Graph Embedding
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are an efficient method for representing heterogeneous knowledge. In KGs, knowledge is represented as triples and transformed into a low-dimensional space using graph embedding techniques, benefiting downstream tasks such as recommender systems and question answering. In real-world scenarios, knowledge graphs are continuously updated with new facts. However, existing KG embedding models only support static graph embeddings, requiring the re-training of the entire graph whenever knowledge updates occur, resulting in time-consuming. There are limited models that support dynamic embedding, which utilizes already trained embeddings to generate representations of new data to improve embedding efficiency. However, these models often ignore the semantic information inherent in the new data itself and the unique structural information in the KG, resulting in low embedding quality. To address this issue, we propose an embedding method specifically designed for dynamic knowledge graphs. Initially, we obtain the semantic representation by quantifying the descriptive information of the added nodes as an initialization vector. Next, to ensure compliance with the graph structure in the KG, we leverage the triple structure of neighboring nodes to the new nodes, and iteratively train the semantic representation to satisfy the structural constraints of KG, resulting in an embedding vector that incorporates both semantic and structural information. We compare our model with existing KG embedding models on two benchmark datasets in link prediction task. The experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves higher efficiency while maintaining the same level of accuracy, thereby validating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Movie Recommendation System Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Traditional recommendation algorithms based on the user's historical behavior and popularity of the product, which generally have the problems of data sparsity and cold start. Knowledge graph technology can provide users with richer and personalized recommendation results by integrating multidimensional features of movies and analyzing the associations between movies. This paper presents a recommendation algorithm which is based on knowledge graph technology, and analyses the requirements on the personalized movie recommendation system. And then based on the study of above, this paper designs the new whole system and then described the system implementation in detail. This recommendation system main functions include: Movies Management, Movies Details, Guess what you like, and Knowledge Graph Visualization. Integrating knowledge graph technology into personalized movie recommendation system can effectively improve the accuracy and interpretability of movie recommendation.

articleTitle: A Non-Euclidean Causal Discovery Algorithm in Metric Spaces
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Causal information is implicit in the spatial characteristics of non-Euclidean data, and recently some researchers have proposed the Non-Euclidean Causal Model (NECM) to describe causal relationships in non-Euclidean data generation. In this paper, we first introduce distance covariance as the criterion for independence testing in the NECM and subsequently define strong or weak correlations between tensor variables containing potential causal relationships. Secondly, we propose a novel causal structure learning algorithm called Distance Covariance-based Non-Euclidean Hybrid Learning (D-NEHL), which can learn causal networks for non-Euclidean data in metric spaces. Finally, we conduct experiments on both simulated data and real stock market data. The results demonstrate that the D-NEHL algorithm exhibits higher accuracy and time performance compared to existing non-Euclidean causal learning methods. It is applicable to various types of non-Euclidean datasets and performs well on traditional Euclidean datasets.

articleTitle: Exploration of Text Classification Algorithms Based on Word Vector Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This article employs Python web scraping techniques to extract text data from videos on Bilibili. It then explores the impact of different text vectorization methods and classification algorithms on the classification results. Initially, various methods such as LDA, Word2vec, Bert, and a fusion of Word2vec and Bert are used to vectorize the text. Subsequently, text classification is carried out using methods like KNN, SVM, and BP, followed by integrated processing of the classification results. For text vectorization, the fused model is used to vectorize the text to get better classification results. In the integrated processing, combining multiple "weak" classifiers to form a "strong" classifier achieves a globally optimal F1 score of 0.9686. In real-world classification problems, it is important to employ the concepts of fusion and integration, leveraging the latest algorithms or tools to enhance classification effectiveness and better handle text categorization tasks.

articleTitle: ME-Net: A Multiscale and Edge-aware Network for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Precision in delineating retinal vessels is crucial for identifying and diagnosing eye diseases. However, retinal blood vessels exhibit significant variation in size and shape, with a vast number of tiny blood vessels distributed at the end of the vascular tree. Additionally, there are often several similar and complex ocular structures and regions surrounding these blood vessels, making this task highly challenging. In this research, we suggest a neural network with multiscale and edge-aware features for retinal vessel segmentation, employing an encoder-decoder architecture. This design enhances the network’s responsiveness to vessel boundaries. Initially, we design a Multiscale Spatial Channel Attention Module (MSCAM) module on top of the encoder to gather essential location information of blood vessels at different scales. Subsequently, we incorporate an Edge-aware Vessel Feature Extraction (EVFE) module into the skip connection to improve the identification of small blood vessel boundaries. Our network’s outstanding segmentation performance is showcased by extensive experiments on two public datasets (DRIVE, IOSTAR), outperforming various mainstream and advanced methods.

articleTitle: Foot Pressure Analysis Based on Flexible Thin Film Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The distribution and changes in plantar pressure are closely related to human health, and can be used to assess the presence of foot diseases. Accurate assessment of plantar pressure distribution plays a preventive and diagnostic role in foot diseases. In order to achieve the function of assessing foot conditions through plantar pressure, the characteristics and differences in plantar pressure variation among different individuals were studied. Flexible and thin-film pressure sensors with array distribution were used to collect plantar data from both healthy individuals and diabetic patients. MATLAB was used to generate pressure distribution maps of average peak pressure, with different colors representing the intensity of pressure in different regions. Python was used to generate line graphs and pie charts. The line graph intuitively shows the pressure distribution in different regions of the foot, while the pie chart presents the proportion of each region’s pressure in the total pressure. Analysis revealed that approximately 50% of the body weight is borne by the heel during the weight-bearing process of standing, with higher pressure on the medial side of the heel compared to the lateral side. The other parts are borne by the first to fifth metatarsal bones. Significant differences were observed in peak plantar pressure between diabetic patients and healthy individuals. The experimental results demonstrate that this study can collect and analyze pressure at different parts of the foot, and identify any abnormal conditions. The study reveals the patterns of peak pressure distribution in the foot, thereby serving the prevention and monitoring of foot diseases, including diabetic foot.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Classification with Bayesian Neural Networks: Improved Training Techniques and Decision Strategies for Reliable AI Support in Uncertainty-Sensitive Tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Bayesian theory is a probabilistic statistical framework for dealing with uncertainty and incomplete information, while neural networks are widely applied in deep learning fields such as image processing. Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) combine Bayesian theory and neural networks to provide more comprehensive predictive results. Although BNNs have significant advantages in expressing model uncertainty, their training methods and network structure design are still to be explored. Effectively training BNNs and exploring their network structure design to enhance predictive performance and computational efficiency are the core of this research. The study aims to improve the performance of BNNs in image classification tasks, specifically including the quantification and utilization of uncertainty to enhance model reliability and decision support capabilities. We use efficient training methods such as variational inference to redesign Bayesian neural networks and conduct deep image recognition training on the CIFAR-10 dataset. The improved training method allows for the rapid and accurate estimation of model weight uncertainty, while the proposed decision strategy utilizes uncertainty information to make reliable decisions. This study demonstrates that BNNs have tremendous potential in addressing real-world uncertainty issues, with the results expected to provide safer AI decision support for risk-sensitive tasks and promote the reliability and practicality of deep learning technology in various critical applications.

articleTitle: XGBoost-Enhanced Prediction and Interpretation of Heart Disease Using SHAP Values
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Heart disease represents a critical challenge to global public health, with its propensity to gravely impact human life and well-being. While current prediction models have achieved relative success, the heterogeneity and complexity inherent in medical data often result in diagnostic inaccuracies when applied practically. There is, therefore, a pressing need for the development of prediction models that are both more accurate and efficient. This article introduces a classification model for heart disease prediction, underpinned by the XGBoost algorithm and informed by authentic medical datasets from the Kaggle platform. To elucidate the predictive decisions of the model, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values are utilized, which provide an interpretive framework for the output. The proposed model exhibits strong predictive capabilities and interpretability, presenting a valuable tool for medical practitioners in the diagnosis and management of heart disease.

articleTitle: Research on Information Propagation Model of Two-Layer Network based on Node Importance
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: At present, breakthroughs have been made in the research of propagation dynamics based on single-layer networks, but there is still a lack of related research on two-layer networks. Therefore, this paper takes the two-layer network as the research object, and constructs a two-layer network information propagation model based on node importance—SnIR. Based on the two-layer network information propagation mode, taking twitter social network as the experimental data, carrying simulation experiments on the SIR model and SnIR, compared and analyzed the information propagation phenomenon, and selected the two evaluation indicators of maximum infection ratio and immune coverage to evaluate the performance of the model. The experimental results show that the information propagation speed is faster, the propagation is more stable, and the information diffusion range is wider on the model proposed in this chapter.

articleTitle: Enhanced Assessment of Auditory Perception Function in Disorders of Consciousness Using a Minimalist Wearable Brain-Computer Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) is a clinical behavioral method for assessing the levels of consciousness and perceptual abilities in patients with Disorders of Consciousness (DOC). However, due to severe impairment of motor functions in DOC patients and subjective factors of clinical evaluators, the misdiagnosis rate of the CRS-R is very high. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) can directly detect patients’ brain activity in response to external stimuli, independent of patients’ behavioral representation, thereby achieving a more objective assessment. In this study, we introduced a minimalist wearable BCI system grounded in the auditory oddball paradigm to enhance assessment of auditory perception function in DOC patients. In the experiments, sinusoidal tones and the complex sound of clapping were selected as standard stimuli occurring frequently and occasional deviant stimuli, respectively. The specific event-related potentials evoked by the auditory stimuli facilitated the assessment of auditory perceptual function. The experimental results indicate that the DOC patients with auditory perception functions can also be detected by the BCI system. As a result, the BCI could serve as a valuable adjunct tool in clinical practice of the CRS-R.

articleTitle: On Early Prediction and Diagnosis of Heart Disease Based on Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This study addresses the early prediction and diagnosis of heart disease using the random forest algorithm to handle many features and perform classification. The study utilized CDC annual survey data related to the health status of 400,000 adults in the United States in 2020, including features such as gender, age, BMI, smoking status, alcohol consumption, history of stroke, and sleep duration. Based on this data, a random forest model was constructed and trained by dividing the data into training and testing sets. Following the model training, performance evaluation was conducted, including the calculation of accuracy and precision metrics. The experimental results demonstrated the excellent accuracy of our random forest model in predicting heart disease. This indicates that it can assist doctors in rapidly and accurately diagnosing and predicting heart disease, thereby improving patient treatment outcomes and quality of life, while also offering new possibilities for heart disease prediction.

articleTitle: A multi-party logistic regression using the Adam method
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) allows multi-party to jointly compute a function while ensuring data security and computation correctness. Nowadays, due to the lack of trust among data holders, various inconveniences arise in data sharing. Secure multi-party computation can partially address such issues by securely enabling computations involving multiple parties’ data while protecting the privacy of each party’s data. In this paper, a secure multi-party Adam method is proposed based on secure multi-party computation, and the non-linear operations in the original scheme are approximated. By optimizing the computation of the power function in the secure multiparty computation protocol, the protocol can compute higher-order Taylor expansions with lower communication complexity and ensuring security. Through the optimization of the secure multi-party computation protocol itself, the proposed multi-party Adam method achieves lower communication overhead and faster convergence speed compared to traditional multi-party gradient descent methods within the same number of iterations.

articleTitle: Motion Planning of Targeted Tea Leaves Harvesting by Manipulator Based on State Parsing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, the application of intelligent robotics in agriculture has been growing, driving the field towards intelligence. Harvesting research has emerged accordingly, with tea picking posing demanding requirements for manipulator motion planning. Challenges like low precision and poor robustness have persisted in robotic tea harvesting research. Hence, motion planning for tea-picking manipulators has become an important topic. This study focuses primarily on motion planning for tea picking tasks using manipulators, proposing a state parsing based approach. We validate its applicability to tea picking and generalizability to small target harvesting. The designed motion planning utilizes optimized algorithms to achieve efficient, accurate and stable tea leaf picking in various environments. The state parsing based planning signifies an innovative solution for small target grasping. It can effectively enhance efficiency, ensure quality, and realize modernization and intelligence of tea production. Meanwhile, it provides new insights into small target robotic grasping research with immense application potential in intelligent agricultural equipment.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Intelligent Inventory System for Small and Micro Enterprise Warehousing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Warehousing for small and micro enterprises has been facing problems such as small warehousing scale, many types of materials, and more scattered placement locations. An intelligent warehousing inventory system was designed by combining visual recognition technology with the inventory module. The system uses image processing and machine vision technology to identify and decode the QR codes on materials and shelves, interact with the inventory module of the warehouse management system, detect whether the material and storage location matches and inventory the quantity of materials, and improve warehouse inventory level. The practical results show that the inventory accuracy of the intelligent inventory system is 98.5%, which can help small and micro enterprises better cope with the challenges in warehouse management, improve inventory efficiency, reduce labor costs, and enhance competitiveness.

articleTitle: Adaptive Latent Distribution Margin GAN for Imbalanced Data Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) has achieved significant development as a result of the development of deep learning. However, the constrained size of FER datasets constrains the generalization capability of expression recognition models, resulting in suboptimal model performance. In addition, the currently available training datasets for FER suffer from imbalances that give preference to certain majority classes, resulting in diminished test accuracy specifically for the minority classes. In this paper, we propose a Adaptive Latent Distribution Margin Generative Adversarial Network (ALDMGAN). It employs a distinct latent distribution model for each class, facilitating a clear demarcation between minority and majority classes. In addition, we propose a objective function that minimizes the distribution disparity between classes, resulting in a closer proximity of their latent distributions. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that ALDMGAN substantially enhances the classification accuracy of unbalanced data.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-MixFaster: A Lightweight Traffic Sign Recognition Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of complex structure and heavy computation of traffic sign recognition algorithm, a lightweight traffic sign recognition algorithm YOLOv8-MixFaster algorithm based on YOLOv8 is proposed in this paper to ensure the detection speed is improved with certain detection accuracy. In this paper, the proposed MixFaster module serves as a lightweight feature extraction component, aiming to enhance the computational efficiency. In addition, in order to alleviate the huge computational load caused by YOLOv8 decoupling head and improve the detection efficiency, SG_Head is proposed in this paper. After the algorithm is lightweight, the accuracy will inevitably decline. In order to improve the recognition accuracy, we also improved the overall structure of YOLOv8 and increased the size of the feature map fed into the recognition head to make it more suitable for small target recognition such as traffic signs. In the data set, we selected the common 45 classification in TT100K(2021). Through experiments, the YOLOv8-MixFaster algorithm achieved an average recognition accuracy of 83.8% in the test set, with a computational load of 11.2GFLOPs and a parameter count of 1.83M. The CPU single-thread inference time is 63.5ms, which is 1.2% higher than the average recognition accuracy of YOLOv8s algorithm, and the calculation amount is reduced by 61%, the number of parameters is reduced by 83.7%, and the inference time is reduced by 31.3%.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Defect Detection Based on Fast Retrieval of Deep Feature
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Defect detection is an important task in the manufacturing industry. With the development of deep learning, unsupervised algorithms are often used to detect the defects of products. When performing unsupervised defect detection, traditional exhaustive search methods often suffer from the low efficiency and high latency. To address this challenge, an inverted file search method is designed to significantly improve the efficiency and decrease the latency of retrieval process. Our inverted file search method is 15 times faster than traditional exhaustive retieval method on large feature databases while effectively capturing various types of defects with less than 1% loss of accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-directional Total Variation Hyperspectral Image Destriping based on Tensor Decomposition and Group Sparsity
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Most of the traditional destriping work is based on matrix domain (band-by-band) processing hyperspectral images, although satisfactory results can be obtained, some important prior conditions are still ignored. In fact, a hyperspectral remote sensing data can be regarded as a third-order tensor, and the space-spectrum Total Variation based on the tensor has been widely used in destriping work. However, the processing of the strip part rarely involves tensor operations. Driven by the high correlation between hyperspectral data in different spectral bands, in this paper, we proposed a multi-directional total variation destriping algorithm based on tensor decomposition and group sparsity. For the target image, a multi-directional full variational regularization constraint is used to ensure piecewise smoothness while preserving continuity between adjacent spectrums. For stripe noise, we adopted low-rank Dicker decomposition and weighted L21 norm joint constraints. Low-rank Dicker decomposition treats stripe noise as a tensor data, which can better describe global correlation; Weighted L21 norm is used to describe group sparsity of stripe noise. A series of experimental results show that our algorithm can effectively remove all kinds of stripe noise while better retaining the detailed information of the target image.

articleTitle: Enhancing Erythemato-Squamous Disease Diagnosis: A Hybrid Approach with SVM SMOTE and Feature-Selection-Based Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The diagnosis of "erythemato-squamous" disease (ESD) is challenging, with complex symptoms and causes making it difficult to diagnose. Misdiagnosis can lead to serious harm to the patient’s health. This paper proposes a method based on SVM SMOTE and feature selection for the Random Forest model (RF). It utilizes SVM SMOTE to synthesize new data for the minority class of diseases, balancing the dataset, and selects important features to construct the RF diagnostic model. The model achieves a test accuracy of 99.50% and an average test accuracy of 98.62% in cross-validation, outperforming the SVM, NB, and DT models constructed in this paper. This paper provides a new, highly accurate approach for the diagnosis of ESD models, with the hope of addressing the model’s shortcomings in future research.

articleTitle: Audio Scene Recognition Algorithms - Based on Topic Models and Graph Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The topic model serves as a contextual analysis model within the text domain, effectively synthesizing contextual content for analysis. Recent research has extended the application of topic models to audio classification, aiming to address performance degradation resulting from significant feature differences in audio at distinct time points. Traditional methods, while achieving some success in describing audio documents, often neglect the exploration of rich information embedded in topics. This oversight hampers the model's ability to effectively capture dynamic semantics within topics, thereby impacting the performance of recognition models. In this study, we leverage a topic model for feature extraction, analyzing and extracting features from long-duration audio. Subsequently, we employ a graph attention network for feature interaction to further enhance the capabilities of the topic audio feature recognition model. The outcome is the development of an audio scene recognition algorithm grounded in both topic models and graph attention networks.

articleTitle: Context-aware DL-based Approach Combining GNN and Attention for CSI-based Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, due to the limitations of GPS in indoor environments, where signals may be obstructed or reflected, significant advancements have been made in indoor localization technologies to address this gap. Among these, fingerprinting localization based on Channel State Information (CSI) has garnered widespread attention owing to its robustness and cost-effectiveness. The inherent nature of deep learning (DL), with its offline training and online positioning capabilities, aligns seamlessly with CSI fingerprinting localization. With the emergence of deep learning techniques, fingerprinting localization has undergone transformative changes. However, most of the current DL-based approaches are inspired by computer vision and natural language processing, implying that they do not fully account for the physical characteristics of CSI. In this paper, we thoroughly consider the physical properties of CSI and design a context-aware approach to embed CSI into a non-Euclidean space for graph-structured learning. Moreover, in feature learning, we separately contemplate the spatial and frequency dimensions, engaging in graph-structured feature learning from distinct physical dimensions. Results on real-world datasets demonstrate that our methodology significantly outperforms state-of-the-art DL-based and meachine learning (ML)-based approaches.

articleTitle: Siamese Network Based CDC For Tile Color Difference Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Tile color difference refers to the inconsistency in surface color of tiles caused by factors such as raw materials or manufacturing processes, which negatively impacts product quality. Traditional tile color difference detection methods often rely on manual visual inspection, which is time-consuming and prone to subjective errors. To address this issue, the paper suggests a Siamese network structure utilizing central difference convolution. Two identical convolutional neural networks are employed to process reference and test samples, and key features are extracted using central difference convolution. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a large dataset containing numerous tile samples is constructed, and detailed experimental evaluations are conducted. The experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements in tile color difference detection tasks using the Siamese network architecture based on central difference convolution. The outcomes of this study are of great significance in enhancing the level of quality management in tile production processes and provide a new approach to image-based color difference detection. Future research can further optimize the network architecture and algorithms, explore more feature representations and optimization strategies to further enhance the performance and practicality of tile color difference detection.

articleTitle: Adaptive recognition of modulated signals based on complex convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Adaptive recognition and of modulated signals play an important position in modern wireless communications. In order to solve the problem of low recognition accuracy of existing models, we propose an complex convolution neural networks(SACNN). Firstly, the modulated signal data is preprocessed using a short-time fast Fourier transform. Then, a self attention mechanism layer is added after the CNN convolutional layer, which utilizes the similarity between features to increase the weight of corresponding features, thereby achieving the goal of improving the accuracy of target recognition. The final experimental results show that the model is able to accurately recognize 11 different modulated signals at high signal-to-noise ratio, and the average recognition rate can reach up to 90.5% without confusion between different modulated signals, and has higher robustness and higher accuracy than other deep neural networks.

articleTitle: Trip Purpose Identification of Urban Residents Based on Taxi GPS Data and POI Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: A series of traffic problems are prominent with the rapid development of society and economy and people’s living standards. It is extremely important to carry out reasonable traffic planning, in which the trip purpose of urban residents is an important reference factor. Base on taxi Global Positioning System(GPS) data of Qingdao, the data is preprocessed, and citizens’ trip purpose is identified by the Random Forest algorithm and other methods in machine learning. Base on the Point of Interest (POI) data of Qingdao, We can also identify the trip purpose by using k-d tree in Nearest Neighbor Search. Results show that the machine learning methods is feasible and achievable to infer the traveling purpose of citizens, and the accuracy of the Random Forest method is the highest, and combined with results of k-d tree to make a comprehensive judgment on the trip purpose of the citizens, the approach which combines GPS and POI data yields the best performance.

articleTitle: Extracting Behavior Events from Epidemic Daily Reports by Combining Deep Learning and Adversarial Training
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Extracting emergencies from network information has become an important means of public security. However, existing event extraction methods rely on large-scale annotated corpora and are difficult to be effectively applied to extract epidemic behavior events, which is a brand-new task of event extraction. Firstly, an epidemic provenance model is defined to comprehensively model epidemic information in epidemic daily reports. On this basis, we propose an epidemic extraction model of epidemic behavior events, called CBEventMine, that combines deep learning and adversarial training. A relatively simple model structure of BiLSTM+CRF+sigmoid is adopted to achieve fast convergence of the model on small sample data, and an adversarial learning mechanism is added to alleviate the overfitting problem of the model in few-slot learning. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model CBEventMine could effectively extract epidemic event than the existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Compressed Representation for 3D Human Pose Estimation using WiFi signal
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Human pose estimation technology has been increasingly applied in many fields, such as user authentication, activity recognition, and health monitoring. The existing human pose estimation methods are mainly based on cameras and wearable sensors, while some works try to use WiFi signal to perceive finegrained human joints in recent years. WiFi antennas collects 1D WiFi signal, while final outputs are 3D images containing human joints. However, directly mapping 1D WiFi signal to 3D image with human skeletons has limitations such as degree of accuracy and high costs of computation resources. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to bridge the gap between WiFi signal and images for single person 3D human pose estimation using commercial WiFi devices, named CRPose. CRPose takes the 1D WiFi data as input and supervised by a teacher network, which outputs the dense representations of 3D human postures. Our experimental evaluation shows that CRPose can localize 14 joints on the human joints skeleton with an average error of 5.1cm, achieving a 55% improvement in accuracy and a 64% time saving in inference stage when compared to widely recognized methods on RF-based 3D human pose estimation.

articleTitle: A Planning Method for Resuming Collaborative Coverage Tasks when Multiple Robot Nodes Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Multi-robot area coverage can improve the efficiency of tasks such as inspections, but how to resume work after some robot nodes fail is a hot and difficult research topic, that is, the self-healing strategy. When a node fails, the area coverage planning algorithm between multiple nodes easily converges to a local solution, resulting in the inability to obtain effective results. Therefore, this study improves the Salp swarm algorithm, an intelligent group planning method, by adding the levy flight strategy. In addition, the artificial potential field (APF) method leads to the problem that the target is unreachable in the path motion planning of a single robot in a group. This study constructed a special repulsive force potential function to improve the algorithm’s performance. The simulation experiments were designed with multi-node coverage, self-healing strategy after node failure, multi-robot motion path visualization, and self-healing strategy factor analysis. The results show that the method we proposed can realize coverage re-planning after node failure in some areas, and is not affected by the size and scope of the area. This achievement can potentially be applied to the field of multi-robot collaborative sensing.

articleTitle: Time-driven Temporal Block-based Correlation Filter for Visual Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Traditional correlation filter algorithms, while pursuing high tracking performance, overlook the reversibility of tracking and fail to utilize the potential for performance improvement through inter-frame information. The existing methods have introduced a temporal block-based strategy, which allows the filter to inherit the discriminability of previous filters while adapting to more drastic object appearance changes and better utilizing interframe information. However, in order to address boundary effects in complex environments and abnormal response maps caused by model degradation during filter update processes, this paper proposes a time-driven temporal block-based correlation filter tracking algorithm called TB-TDCF. It combines the strategy of temporal blocks with a time regularization term and incorporates it into the base model to ensure that correlation filtering maintains similarity with previous filters during model updating. This procedure effectively suppresses degradation and updates anomalies caused by abnormal response maps, thereby improving accuracy and robustness of the tracking model over long duration tracking processes. Through extensive comparative experiments on datasets such as UAV123, DTB70, and UAVDT-M, this paper validates the superiority of our algorithm in terms of success rate and precision accuracy.

articleTitle: A Method for Extracting Information from Long Documents that Combines Large Language Models with Natural Language Understanding Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Information extraction is a very important task in natural language processing and is widely used in various industries, but due to the ever-changing types of documents, there are still challenges in terms of extraction effectiveness in practical applications. In previous research, traditional AI models were commonly used to address the issue of information extraction from long documents. However, due to challenges related to input length and the capability to understand the semantics of extended texts, the results have consistently fallen short of expectations and have not been practically implemented in industrial production.In this paper, we propose a solution for extracting information from long document based on large language model. While possessing the ability of long-text semantic understanding of large language models, it also effectively alleviates the hallucinations of large language models and the problem of uncontrollable output results through discriminative methods. Compared with other general methods, our approach has achieved significant performance improvement on the long-text dataset we collected. Additionally, our approach is reproducible and can be easily and quickly customized and adapted to other scenarios.

articleTitle: K-nearest Neighbors Ratio Sum Discriminant Analysis Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: As the dimensionality of data processed in the field of machine learning continues to increase, the issue of dimensional catastrophe often arises, necessitating the reduction of data dimensions. Traditional methods for dimensionality reduction typically construct trace ratio problems to optimize solutions based on data variance, but these problems tend to be biased towards smaller variances. The ratio sum criterion addresses this problem by transforming the trace ratio problem into a ratio sum form, thereby preventing subspaces from being projected into directions with smaller variances. However, it primarily focuses on the global variance of the data, neglecting the preservation of local characteristics. To address this limitation and preserve the local characteristics of the data, a novel algorithm called K-Nearest Neighbor Ratio Sum Discriminant Analysis (K-RSDA) is proposed. This algorithm combines k-nearest neighbor composition with the ratio sum algorithm to construct intra-class and inter-class graphs within the data. By doing so, the K-RSDA algorithm enables the ratio sum approach to effectively handle multimodal data and enhance the dimensionality reduction performance. Experiments on several small datasets in the UCI database and face datasets such as Pose27, UMIST, LFW were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: GRU Prediction Method For Digital Cryptocurrency Prices
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, digital cryptocurrencies based on blockchain technology have been widely used globally. However, the huge volatility and high risk of cryptocurrency prices pose challenges for investors. To address this issue, predicting the prices of digital cryptocurrencies has become a research focus. However, most existing studies mainly focus on Bitcoin price prediction. This paper proposes a GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) model-based method for predicting the price of Dogecoin, a popular emerging cryptocurrency. The choice of Dogecoin is motivated by its high price volatility and prediction difficulty as a relatively new cryptocurrency. The GRU model is a variant of the recurrent neural network (RNN) that has better prediction performance compared to the LSTM model. With this method, we can effectively predict the price of Dogecoin, reducing investment risks for investors and providing reference for policymakers in regulating the digital currency market.

articleTitle: Big Data Visualization Analysis of Rice Seedling Quantity Based on UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to reduce the labor cost and improve the efficiency of rice basic seedling statistics, a statistical method based on computer vision was designed. This paper introduced big data of rice spectrum and mixed pixels, established a basic seedling number inversion model, and drew a basic seedling density map, which effectively improved the statistical accuracy of the basic seedling number of rice, saved the labor cost, and intuitively experienced the basic seedling density of rice, and guided the fertilization and nitrogen application work in the later stage according to the requirements. To achieve the purpose of saving fertilizer and increasing yield in the process of rice planting. In this study, two methods were used to retrieve the number of basic rice seedlings. The first method was based on the pixel binary classification of Normalized Vegetation index (NDVI), visible Vegetation index (VDVI) and green Normalized Vegetation Index (GNDVI), with the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) being 0.782, 0.767 and 0.744, respectively. The root mean square errors (RMSE) were 12.44, 12.85 and 13.48, respectively. The other method is a hybrid pixel decomposition method based on fully constrained least squares with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.897 and an RMSE of 8.53. Comprehensive analysis shows that the seedling number inversion model based on hybrid pixel decomposition has higher accuracy

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Based Grassland Net Primary Productivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Grassland resource monitoring is an important element of grassland ecological monitoring and management, with the aim of grasping the basic situation of grasslands and providing strong data support for the formulation of scientific grassland environmental protection and management measures in the future. This paper focuses on the grassland region of northern Shaanxi, China, aiming to study the long-term spatial and temporal patterns of net primary productivity (NPP) in the region, the response mechanism of NPP to climatic factors, and the future trends of NPP under the existing environmental drivers. Using remote sensing data such as Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), meteorology and solar radiation, were used to derive the distribution of NPP in northern Shaanxi, China, during 2010-2020 using the improved CASA model, and the effects of meteorological factors on it were analyzed by correlation analysis. The coupled CASA and CA-Markov model were used to simulate the future trends of NPP and predict future changes in the study area at the pixel level. The results showed that the NPP of grassland in northern Shaanxi, China, generally showed an increasing trend during 2010-2020; NPP had a significant correlation with precipitation, mainly positive, with a correlation coefficient of 0.21; The Kappa coefficient achieved a value of 0.7263, indicating good applicability of the model and its potential use in studying the future change trend of NPP.

articleTitle: Cross-Person Human Activity Recognition Method Based on the HARG Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, Sensor-based human activity recognition technology has found widespread applications in various fields. Recently, Transformer and its variant models, further improving the effectiveness of activity recognition models. However, almost all established models assume that the training and test data maintain data distribution consistency. In practical applications, due to differences in body types, activity styles, and habits, test data distribution changes, leading to a sharp drop in model recognition performance. In this paper, we integrate the Domain-Invariant and the Domain-Specific Feature Module, proposing the Deep Adaptive Domain Feature Module that focuses on deep-level domain features. This is a Domain Generalization-based representation learning that can effectively improve the model’s generalization performance. Specifically, we use Transformer and CNN as the backbone networks, adopt a novel parallelized network structure, proposed the Human Activity Recognition Generalization (HARG) cross-Person human activity recognition model. We systematically evaluate the proposed model on UCI-HAR and Opportunity public datasets, the experiments show that the HARG model has an absolute advantage in cross-domain activity recognition, outperforming current models in recognition performance.

articleTitle: Research on low-dose CT image enhancement algorithm based on CycleGAN improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Low-dose CT imaging has a wide range of applications in the field of medical imaging. However, problems such as noise and low contrast in low-dose CT images pose challenges to the diagnosis and analysis of the images. Therefore, researchers have been working on developing and improving low-dose CT image enhancement methods to improve image quality and feasibility of clinical applications. Aiming at the problems of insufficient image feature extraction and large number of network parameters in CT images by CycleGAN, this thesis proposes an improved low-dose CT image enhancement network based on CycleGAN. A Shallow Feature pre-Extraction Module, which can extract rich semantic information, is designed to enhance the CycleGAN generator’s ability to extract image features in CT images; and some ordinary convolutions in the generator are replaced by Depthwise Separable Convolution with a smaller number of parameters to reduce the network parameters. The experimental results show that the improved CycleGAN exhibits better performance in terms of structural detail preservation, noise and artifacts suppression compared to both the traditional algorithm and other unsupervised algorithms.

articleTitle: Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-Based Proportional Computation Offloading With User Equipment in Smart Home Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The growing adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) applications has resulted in a surge in the offloading of time-sensitive and computationally intensive tasks from IoT devices to mobile edge computing (MEC) servers. In this article, we survey the task partition strategy in a smart home edge computing network with multiple user equipments (UEs) and edge servers (ESs), where each UE runs IoT application and generates computation task periodically. The generated task is allowed to be broken down into several proportions then offloaded to ESs following a task partition strategy designed to minimize both execution latency and energy consumption. We first formulate the task partition problem as a nonlinear programming problem. Subsequently, we introduce an algorithm based on multiagent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) for UEs to optimize their offloading strategies. In the proposed approach, each User Equipment leverages its local observations as input for an actor network, which generates a task partitioning strategy. Simultaneously, a critic network is trained to enhance the performance of task partitioning. Through our simulations, the performance of the proposed algorithm has been confirmed to surpass that of alternative methods in terms of minimizing both delay and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Pre-trained Language Model for Chinese Frame Semantic Parsing based on Electric Power Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the operational landscape of the electric power industry, a wealth of events, operations, and fault reports generates substantial textual data. The application of frame semantic parsing to the power grid system presents challenges, especially given the distinctive characteristics of Chinese text, including entity ambiguity, word segmentation issues, and a misalignment with knowledge in the power systems field. In response to these challenges, we introduce an innovative pipeline specifically designed for Chinese semantic analysis based on an electric power dataset, showcasing significant enhancements over the baseline. This research strives to drive technological advancements, fostering a more sophisticated understanding of textual data within the intricate domain of the Chinese electric power industry, with a particular focus on natural language processing.

articleTitle: Improving BMRC Based on Joint Classifier for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Aspect sentiment triplet extraction(ASTE) is an extremely difficult subtask in aspect-based sentiment analysis. The ASTE task aims to extract triplets of aspect, opinion, and sentiment polarity from review sentences. Bidirectional machine reading comprehension (BMRC) is the current method to settle triplet extraction based on the machine reading comprehension (MRC) paradigm. This method can effectively settle the ASTE task. However, due to the use of shared classifiers, it will cause query conflicts and there will be a problem of reduced probability when predicting answers. Therefore, this paper proposes an improving BMRC based on a joint classifier for aspect sentiment triplet extraction, while adding a balanced span prediction module (BSPM). The joint classifier can effectively settle the query conflict issue and exploit the correlation between subtasks. The balanced span prediction module can make the predicted probabilities of opinion, aspect, and aspect-opinion pairs more consistent with the expectations of the model. We have conducted enough experiments on four benchmark datasets, where our models achieve more significant improvements over the baseline models.

articleTitle: Optimization of Transmission in Heterogeneous Integrated Networks for Active Distribution Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The distribution range of active distribution sub-stations is extensive, and their topology structures are diverse. The presence of numerous distributed power access points poses significant challenges to observability and operational control, necessitating the urgent strengthening of communication infrastructure. Traditional optical fiber dedicated networks require substantial economic and manpower investments, while relying solely on power line communication and low-power wireless communication methods is insufficient to meet various communication requirements. In response to this, this paper proposes a heterogeneous integrated network transmission optimization method that combines power line communication and wireless communication for active distribution substations. In the context of supporting multiple communication paths in heterogeneous CRANs, the unreliable communication caused by interference is avoided, and corresponding solving methods are proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can identify the optimal transmission path from any source node to the central aggregation node that satisfies the performance requirements, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Network Pruning based Target Detection Model for CenterFusion
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success in the field of object detection. However, efficiently deploying these models in embedded systems still poses challenges related to model size and computational complexity. This paper focuses on optimizing the CenterFusion model through the application of the weight-based L1 norm pruning method. We adopt a targeted network pruning approach, specifically addressing the Centernet component within CenterFusion, to reduce the model’s parameter count and complexity, making it more suitable for resource-constrained environments in embedded systems. The innovation of this research lies in the inaugural application of the weight-based L1 norm pruning method to the CenterFusion model. Additionally, it incorporates two iterations of pruning based on weight changes, allowing for further compression of the network model. This provides a practical solution for the efficient deployment of the model on embedded platforms. Testing before and after pruning shows a reduction in the model size by 31.86% and 52.94%, with an overall accuracy loss of only 3.18%. The pruned model significantly reduces volume while maintaining object detection performance. This suggests that the pruned network achieves a lightweight object detection model, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of deploying advanced object detection technology in embedded systems.

articleTitle: FSCPUnet: A Blind Denoising U-shaped Network Based on Swin Transformer and Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Image denoising is a challenging and practical task that has long fascinated computer vision researchers. In past denoising efforts, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have been the most commonly used network model. In recent years, however, transformers have achieved considerable success in various visual tasks, including image restoration. Nevertheless, transformers still have limitations in extracting local image features compared to CNNs. Therefore, we aim to effectively combine Transformers and CNNs, harnessing their respective global and local feature extraction capabilities by proposing a novel image feature extraction module called SCPB and embedding it in a U-shaped network to enhance the multi-scale feature extraction capabilities. This gives rise to the FSCPUNet (Flexible Swin Transformer CAConv Parallel Unet) for image blind denoising. Furthermore, the model incorporates a noise estimation network to adapt to different noise levels, addressing the challenge of image blind denoising. Experimental results show that the FSCPUNet proposed in this paper outperforms existing denoising models in various denoising tasks.

articleTitle: Multi-Encoder with Entity-Aware Embedding Framework for Distantly Supervised Relation Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Distantly supervised relation extraction (DSRE) inherently faces challenges arising from labeling noise due to the distant supervision assumption. Most existing studies employ Piece-wise CNN (PCNN) to extract semantic features from sentences, often neglecting to comprehensively capture contextual features. As a consequence, valuable information is lost, leading to a decline in relation prediction performance. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Encoder with Entity-Aware Embedding Framework for Distantly Supervised Relation Extraction (MEEA), designed to enhance the prediction of entity relations by effectively capturing comprehensive contextual features. Specifically, MEEA employs a novel entity-aware word embedding method that employs an attention fusion mechanism to integrate relative position information and information of two entities, which can emphasize the importance of entity pair in RE. Meanwhile, we adopt a multi-encoder framework that utilizes PCNN and two distinct sentence encoders to extract diverse features. Subsequently, these features are effectively fused through an attention fusion mechanism to capture global contextual dependencies comprehensively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed MEEA framework exhibits significant enhancements over previous methods when applied to NYT10, GDS, and Wiki-20m datasets.

articleTitle: MTCNet: A Multi-scaled Temporal Convolution Network for Sleep Apnea Detection from Single-lead ECG Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a common sleep disorder caused by decreased blood oxygen saturation during sleep. Polysomnography is the gold standard for early detection. Because of the complicated operation and high price, it is gradually out of the public view. In recent years, single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signal detection sleep apnea methods based on deep learning have significantly progressed. This paper proposes a multi-scale temporal convolutional network (MTCNet) to detect sleep apnea. MTCNet uses multi-scale convolutional networks to capture fine-grained and coarse-grained features. This design enhances the analysis of characteristics associated with sleep apnea. The proposed MTCNet model significantly improved sleep apnea detection compared to previous methods. In our proposed model, the accuracy reached 91.5%, and the average sensitivity and specificity reached 85.8% and 95.0%, respectively.

articleTitle: Flink Stream Big Data Parallel Operator Design and Topsis Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The process of streamlining big data processing encounters several challenges, including managing extensive data volumes and ensuring high real-time performance. Flink has emerged as the favored technical solution in the realm of big data streaming processing due to its provision of numerous parallel operators. However, the effective design of these parallel operators and the performance evaluation process are pivotal for achieving efficient streaming data processing. Consequently, this study has formulated a series of parallel operators and assessed their performance using the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (Topsis) algorithm. The findings of this investigation emphasize the significance of operator design in streamlining big data processing. This research offers substantial support and serves as a valuable reference for resource optimization and performance evaluation. These outcomes have profound implications, not only in managing vast real-time data streams but also in the development of applications and systems aimed at addressing the challenges posed by large-scale data

articleTitle: 3D ConvNet+: A lightweight adaptive network for 3D medical image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Recent advancements in 3D medical ViTs, have achieved the best performance on multiple 3D volume constitutes benchmark data for three-dimensional medical image segmentation. The success of these models is attributed to their large receptive fields and extensive model parameters facilitated by non-local self-attention mechanisms. In order to emulate the behavior of large receptive fields exhibited by learning methods, this work introduces a novel lightweight volumetric convolutional network named 3D ConvNet+. Drawing inspiration from the Swin Transformer, the network reexamines volumetric convolutions with large kernel sizes, starting, for instance, from 7×7×7, to achieve a larger global receptive field.Additionally, to better utilize multiscale information, researchers introduce the Lightweight Hybrid Aggregation (LHA) module. LHA leverages adaptive fusion mechanisms with dynamic weight adjustments, providing a crucial advantage to image segmentation structural models with its lightweight and efficient design. We believe that this research methodology will contribute significantly to the academic discourse and practical applications in the field of intelligent segmentation. Furthermore, we anticipate that it will stimulate further in-depth research, fostering advancements in this domain.

articleTitle: YOLOv7-VD: An Algorithm for Vehicle Detection in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Addressing the problems that existing vehicle detection algorithms do not have high detection accuracy in complex scenes, as well as the problem that the parameters of the deep learning model are large and occupy too much computer video memory, an improved algorithm, YOLOv7-VD, based on YOLOv7, is proposed. First, to simplify the operation of the network, the ghost convolution module will be introduced on the feature extraction network. Second, the spatial pyramid pooling cross stage partial channel-channel shuffle (SPPCSPCS) module is proposed. To improve the fusion of feature maps with different depths, this module adds channel shuffling to the spatial pyramid pooling structure. Once again, the network utilizes a 9x9 convolution kernel to replace certain 3x3 convolution kernels. This is done to enhance the network's active sensory patch and shape bias, and a 1x1 convolution is used to adjust the input feature layer to reduce model size and delay. Finally, the article introduces the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) attention mechanism that enhances the feature representation of the target being detected while removing redundant convolutional kernels and reducing parameters. The experimental tests demonstrate that the enhanced YOLOv7 improves mAP@0.5 by 2.01% over the baseline algorithm on the BDD 10K dataset, improves accuracy by 5.18%, and reduces the total number of parameters by 15.07%.

articleTitle: 2-D general network based on channel-space attention for medical image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: General and effective medical image segmentation methods achieve pixel-level accurate segmentation of lesions or organs. Existing 2-D networks have difficulty in exploiting complementary information among modalities on multi-modal segmentation tasks. This study proposes a multi-scale general medical image segmentation 2-D network (MCS-Net) based on CNN and Transformer. Specifically, a channel-space attention module is designed to independently group feature maps and calculate channel attention weights within each group, which successfully fuses channel information among different scales. We also introduce a multi-scale convolution module to acquire more abundant multi-receptive field features, which is beneficial for extracting multi-scale features and obtaining fine-grained local information. Extensive experiments on typical single-modal and multi-modal image segmentation tasks demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of MCS-Net and show that our approach is significantly superior to current state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Feature Memory and Deep Cross Network for Parameter Prediction of Offshore drilling
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The Rate of Penetration (ROP) is a critical indicator of drilling efficiency in offshore drilling engineering. Accurately predicting ROP can significantly enhance drilling efficiency and reduce enterprise costs, making it a crucial topic in the oil industry. In this paper, we propose a deep learning method called the Feature Memory and Deep Cross Network (FMDCN). This model has the unique ability to remember important features and analyze time-series data, resulting in a more accurate prediction of ROP. Our experiments, conducted on real datasets, demonstrate that FMDCN consistently outperforms general time-series models, showing a smaller prediction error.

articleTitle: SCLFD: A Novel Latency Fault Detection Approach for Service Composition
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Due to the uncertainty of the cloud environment, the response time of service inherently exhibits fluctuations and randomness, making it challenging to ensure the accuracy of latency fault detection of service composition. Therefore, this paper proposes a latency fault detection approach for service composition. Firstly, a global response time monitoring framework is introduced by analyzing the execution process of service composition. Secondly, according to the acquired monitoring data, an inference algorithm based on evidential reasoning(ER) rule for response time anomaly alarm is designed. We evaluate the approach with an actual service composition scenario about elevator traction wire rope design. Experimental results show the accuracy of the proposed approach can achieve 91.57%, significantly outperforming traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multiple Linear Regression for Price Prediction: A PCA-Integrated Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The conventional multiple linear regression model is limited by its inability to process high-dimensional datasets, susceptibility to multicollinearity, and challenges in modeling non-linear relationships. To address these issues, alternative methodologies are required. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a widely employed technique for dimensionality reduction that transforms high-dimensional datasets into lower-dimensional spaces, thereby mitigating the issues associated with high-dimensionality and extracting principal features for dimension reduction. Additionally, PCA can alleviate multicollinearity concerns, enhancing the reliability of regression models. In this study, we employ PCA in conjunction with multiple linear regression to predict prices, achieving notably precise outcomes. This hybrid method not only elevates the accuracy of predictions but also provides substantial support in applications such as stock price forecasting, market pricing strategies, product positioning, and profit maximization. The integration of PCA with multiple linear regression holds significant practical relevance, offering a methodological advancement that can improve the decision-making accuracy and efficiency for investors.

articleTitle: Big Data Analysis Of Female Dysmenorrhea Based On Multiple Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Dysmenorrhea is one of the most common gynecological disorders, and when it is severe, it may have many adverse effects on the patient's life and work. In order to assist the treatment of dysmenorrhea and reduce the pain of patients as much as possible, this paper carries out a questionnaire survey on all the females in a university in Qingdao City. Based on the collected data, a variety of machine learning models including association rule, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), decision tree, and random forest are set up to find out the relevant factors affecting dysmenorrhea, and a dysmenorrhea prediction model is set up and optimized. The experimental results show that the various machine learning methods proposed in this paper have good effects on studying the causes of dysmenorrhea and predicting the occurrence of dysmenorrhea.

articleTitle: Price Prediction and Analysis Based on the LightGBM Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Price forecasting is widely used in many fields.lt is of great significance for economic development to find out the model and method of predicting price accurately.Traditional methods of predicting prices include market comparison, income restoration, and cost estimation, but these methods require a significant amount of human and material resources and usually fail to predict housing prices accurately due to the influence of numerous factors. Therefore, this paper aims to use the LightGBM regression model and LGBMRegressor algorithm for the prediction and analysis of housing prices. We collected a large amount of data on second-hand housing prices and preprocessed the data to eliminate entries with missing values. Subsequently, we performed a general descriptive statistical analysis of the data and established feature data and label data based on different characteristics such as region, age of the house, nearby geographical conditions, cultural and traffic factors. Finally, we divided the dataset and made model predictions. The experimental results show that the predicted values of the regression model are basically consistent with the actual fluctuations in housing prices, allowing for relatively accurate predictions.

articleTitle: Design of a Full Process License Plate Detection System Based on Deep Learning and Cloud Platform System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: As digital technology continued to evolve, license plate detection systems became crucial auxiliary systems for daily parking management. However, research on non-fixed license plate detection systems had long been a blind spot in related technological exploration. To address this issue, this paper employed deep learning technology to detect license plates at angles, in blurred conditions, and under low light, leveraging cloud technology for data processing. To meet data security and practical production requirements, the system stored and pushed detection results to a WeChat public account (mobile platform) through a cloud platform. Pushing results to the mobile platform via the cloud platform yielded excellent performance, demonstrating significant engineering application value.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Facial Attribute Editing Method based on Autoencoder in StyleGAN Latent Space
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Currently, facial attribute editing based on StyleGAN latent space has achieved great success, but it suffers from problems such as attribute entanglement and identity information loss in real facial attribute editing. To address these issues, this paper suggests utilizing an autoencoder network to extract the high-level identity information from the latent code, and then reconstruct the latent code following the incorporation of conditional semantic information. The embedded conditional semantic information aims to guide the autoencoder to achieve facial attribute editing. In the training process, reconstruction loss and conditional loss are introduced to constrain the autoencoder network, so that it can reconstruct the editing results that keep the identity information unchanged and meet the preset attribute change conditions.
