The experiments show that this method achieves facial attribute editing with no entanglement, controllability, and retention of identity features in real facial data. In several quantitative evaluation indicators, proposed method is better than the recent methods.

articleTitle: Measuring the Influencing Factors for Enterprises Adoption of Big Data: Prioritizing By Decision making process by using Dematel-ANP Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In this research study, we can systematically analyze and prioritize the various factors that impact an organization’s decision to adopt big data technology. Further, this paper examines the influencing factors for enterprises adoption of big data and establishes an indicator system based on the Motivation-Opportunity- Ability (MOA) model. In addition, the study finds that the MOA model can effectively explain enterprises motivations, opportunities, and abilities in applying big data. The DEMATEL technique, integrated with the Analytic Network Process (ANP), is used to construct the network relationship map, and the relationships between each factor are analyzed. This research contributes to understanding the factors that affect the adoption of big data in enterprises and provides a theoretical basis for future research in this area.

articleTitle: An Attention-Based CNN Algorithm to Predict Hard-To-Predict Branches
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In modern high-performance microprocessors, branch prediction is crucial for mitigating performance losses due to pipeline stalls. Incorrect predictions result in CPU instruction pipeline halts, mainly from a few systematically challenging complex branches (Hard-To-Predict, H2P) where current techniques lack accuracy. Traditional TAGE-based branch prediction struggles with noisy complex branches and scalability issues. As application scales and types grow, traditional high-performance processor branch prediction faces challenges. This paper introduces SS-CNN: a Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)-based complex branch prediction algorithm. It identifies relevant branches in branch history using CNN and extracts features for prediction. Additionally, attention mechanisms and slice structures are incorporated. Optimization enhances the model’s ability to extract features and identify relevant branches, improving prediction accuracy. Experimental results show SS-CNN achieves 86.46% accuracy for complex branches, a 1.01% improvement over TAGE SC L. SS-CNN reduces average MPKI by 4.18% compared to TAGE SC L, signifying enhanced accuracy, fewer interruptions, increased throughput, and lower power consumption, improving computer architecture performance.

articleTitle: Incorporating Large Language Models into Named Entity Recognition: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) is a critical task in natural language processing, involving the identification and classification of entities in text. Traditional approaches to NER, such as rule-based methods and supervised machine learning, faced limitations in adapting to diverse domains and languages due to the need for large labeled datasets. Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT3, which undergo vast pretraining, demonstrate the promising ability to substantially improve NER beyond supervised baselines as evidenced by over a 100% increase in F1 score on domain-specific evaluation corpora.This survey comprehensively examines the pivotal roles and methodologies of LLMs in NER. It provides a thorough analysis of two key techniques: in-context learning and fine-tuning. In-context learning enables quick NER task resolution without major model changes, while fine-tuning offers significant improvements, especially in domain-specific applications. The survey also covers essential resources, including NER corpora, LLM types, and methods of fine-tuning. It addresses challenges related to computational resources and model size. The survey concludes by outlining potential future research directions, emphasizing LLMs’ contributions to advancing NER technologies.

articleTitle: Moment Distribution of Hyper-Erlang Distribution and Its Approximation Application
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Moment distributions can be used to study many important problems in the field of social sciences, such as the Gini coefficient of residents’ income, Lorenz curve, etc. The set of Hyper-Erlang distributions is a dense subset of the set of non-negative probability distribution functions, which has a wide applicability, so Hyper-Erlang distributions are chosen as the object of this study. In this paper, we give the analytical expression of the moment distribution of HyperErlang distribution and prove that the moment distribution function of Hyper-Erlang distribution is closed within the set of Hyper-Erlang distribution. Combined with the HyperErlang distribution parameter estimation algorithm, eight commonly used distributions are fitted, and the practicality and effectiveness of the Hyper-Erlang moment distribution method proposed in this paper are verified through the comparison of the original moment distribution of the commonly used distributions and the approximation effect of the Hyper-Erlang moment distribution. The approach proposed in this paper can be used to give a moment distribution expression for any data, and valid approximate moment distribution expressions for all types of probability distributions for which no analytical moment distribution expression can be derived.

articleTitle: A Sparse Feature Clustering-based Stain Normalization Method for Pathological Images
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Gold standard for diagnosing malignant tumors is pathological diagnosis, and digital pathology is current trend. Difference in stain process of pathological slides and lack of standardization in digitization of pathological images have posed challenges to development of digital pathology due to stain variation in images. Therefore, this paper proposed a new stain normalization method for pathological images based on sparse feature clustering. Based on CycleGAN, this method effectively addressed the problem of inadequate representation of template image in traditional stain normalization methods. Simultaneously, by adopting a sparse K-means clustering algorithm, this method effectively handled significant stain variations in datasets. In comparison, SSIM and PSNR of this method were 0.96 and 32.62, respectively. These values were significantly superior to those of Reinhard and Vahadane methods. Moreover, this method obtained better visual effects, which would provide guidance for auxiliary clinicopathological diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Pyramid Network Using Scale Agnostic Attention for Single Image Reflection Removal
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Single Image Reflection Removal (SIRR) is a hot topic in downstream tasks of computer vision, with the aim of eliminating undesirable reflections in degraded images taken through glass. However, due to the ill-posed property of SIRR and the lack of large-scale real world mixture images contaminated by reflections, existing methods degrade on real datasets and suffer from the problem of reflection residue. In this work, we propose an efficient SIRR pyramid model that can robustly recover real images degraded by reflections. Specifically, our network uses a Nonlinear Activation Free Network (NAFNet) as a baseline, a variant of U-Net, which is capable of extracting feature maps of different scales. Furthermore, to learn the pixel-level long-distance feature correspondence between multi-scale features, a pyramid fusion module based on scale-agnostic attention has been embedded into the baseline. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our model.

articleTitle: Proportional Feature Pyramid Network for Lane Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Lane detection under extreme conditions presents a highly challenging task that requires capturing each crucial pixel to predict the complex topology of lane lines and differentiate the various lane types. Existing methods predominantly rely on deep feature extraction networks with substantial parameters or the fusion of multiple prediction modules, resulting in large model sizes, embedding difficulties, and slow detection speeds. This paper proposes a Proportional Feature Pyramid Network(P-FPN) through fusing the weights into the FPN for lane detection. In our method, the high-level features are explored to predict lanes coarsely while local- detailed features are leveraged to improve localization accuracy. Extensive experiments on the widely used lane detection dataset, CULane dataset, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the competitive results compared with several state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Identifying Antibiotic Resistance in Pathogenic Bacteria through SVM and Neural Network Predictive Models
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The development and widespread implementation of technologies for detecting antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria are both urgent and instrumental for advancements in biology and medicine. This paper presents a study where DNA base sequences are utilized as sample data, categorized into susceptible and resistant groups. A predictive model based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) is employed to accurately distinguish between these groups by identifying specific DNA sequence loci. Additionally, a comparative analysis with neural network models is conducted to refine the classification and prediction methods for pathogenic bacteria. The findings indicate that the SVM model is effective in classifying and predicting the base sequence loci that are significantly associated with genetic mutations leading to antibiotic resistance in bacteria.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Tianjin Earthquake Warning Network System Based on Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The traditional seismic monitoring network is a product of the era of small data. After an earthquake occurs, there are usually more than ten observation station data participating in event analysis. These data are stored using traditional MySQL databases. The calculation process often adopts a human-computer interaction method. But with the implementation of early warning projects, high-density seismic observation networks have been built. This new type of seismic network is a strong support for second magnitude earthquake warning. But at the same time, it also generated a massive amount of observational data, the earthquake monitoring network has entered the era of big data. Traditional data storage and calculation methods do not meet the needs of earthquake warning systems, because earthquake warning systems need to analyze a large amount of data and quickly produce results. During the implementation of the warning project, Tianjin Earthquake Agency designed a earthquake warning network system based on cloud computing. The project team designed the overall system architecture using SaaS technology, and used a simple intensity meter to collect strong motion data. The system adopts concurrent filtering and reception technology to timely collect and process massive data produced by seismic stations. The project team has designed a software architecture for the seismic wave simulation display model based on web pages. Business personnel use High Chart JS software in the browser to simulate and display seismic waveforms. The system can carry out automatic detection and management of earthquake event triggering. Through the evaluation of the system and the analysis of historical earthquakes, it has been proven that the system can accurately provide early warning of earthquake occurrence, which is superior to the performance of existing earthquake warning systems.

articleTitle: The Problem of Goods Distribution Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Goods distribution is of great significance in realizing economies of scale and saving transportation costs. Therefore, this paper aims to explore how to use genetic algorithm to minimize costs in order to achieve the objective function of goods distribution. Firstly, this paper introduces the related concepts of genetic algorithm, and introduces the related concepts such as initializing population, calculating fitness function, selection, crossover and mutation by expounding the general steps of genetic algorithm. Secondly, this paper describes the problem of goods distribution and puts forward the objective function and constraint conditions. Then, using genetic algorithm and MATLAB design program, the goods distribution problems are realized one by one. Finally, the simulation results of this program are analyzed.

articleTitle: Decrypting the Chao-based Image Encryption via A Deep Autoencoding Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In this work, as a proof of concept, we develop a simple yet effective deep autoencoding approach to attack the chaos-based image encryption algorithm. Specifically, we first project chaos-based encrypted images into the low-dimensional feature space. In the manifold, essential information of plain images can be largely preserved. A deconvolutional generator is then utilized to regenerate decrypted images perceptually similar to plain images in the high-dimensional image space. For the first time, we show the feasibility of attacking chaos-based encryption methods in a key-independent manner, which is fundamentally different from traditional image encryption attacks. Given chaos-based encrypted images, a well-trained decryption model can automatically reconstruct plain images with high visual fidelity. In both static-key and dynamic-key experiments, we successfully attack several chaos-based algorithms on the MNIST dataset and show that decrypted images are perceptually recognizable to both human eyes and intelligent models. Importantly, this study demonstrates the potential of employing deep learning approaches to crack image encryption algorithms.

articleTitle: A Novel Data Statistical Analysis Method Based on Hyper-Erlang Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Selecting the appropriate probability distribution can be a challenging task when using parametric methods for statistical analysis of specific data. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method of analyzing the data using the Hyper-Erlang distribution. This distribution is a dense subset of all probability distributions on the non-negative real axis and is both easy to analyze and compute. This paper discusses the dense properties of the Hyper-Erlang distribution and the parameter estimation method based on the expectation maximization algorithm, and verifies the validity of the proposed method using the actual income data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Perceptron-Based Branch Predictor
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: As the demand for computer performance continues to increase in society, along with the escalating requirements of complex software for high-performance hardware, the efficiency of processor instruction execution also needs to be continuously improved. However, the existing TAGE_SC_L predictor suffers from reduced prediction accuracy when dealing with branches exhibiting significant noise. To address this issue, we propose a perceptron-based branch predictor aimed at enhancing the recognition efficiency of relevant branches, thereby improving prediction accuracy and further enhancing processor execution efficiency. We conducted a series of experiments using SPEC CPU 2006 as a benchmark, and the results showed that our predictor improved prediction accuracy, reduced pipeline stalls, and effectively enhanced processor execution efficiency compared to state-of-the-art branch predictors with complex branch prediction accuracy as the baseline.

articleTitle: Optimization Methods for Random Forest Models in Early Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Diabetes affects approximately 537 million people worldwide, accounting for 10.5% of the total population. It has a significant impact on individuals' physical and mental health, highlighting the urgent need for low-cost and effective screening methods. This study focuses on using random forest models for early diabetes prediction. We compare and analyze the results using cross-validation, grid search optimization, and polynomial feature engineering methods to calculate the hyperparameters of the random forest model. These optimization techniques effectively improve the prediction accuracy of the random forest model, enabling more accurate identification of early-stage diabetes patients and promoting diabetes prevention, diagnosis, and early treatment.

articleTitle: Social Recommendation Algorithm Based on Fusion Graph Convolutional Neural Network and Gated Recurrent Unit Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This paper proposes a fusion model named FGCN-GRU (Fusion Graph Convolutional Neural network and Gated Recurrent Unit network) to predict users' ratings on items. Firstly, FGCN-GRU constructs a new graph convolutional neural network by regarding users' ratings on items as relative ratings and introduces the GRU network by considering the fact that the user’s interest in items will change over time. Then the improved graph convolutional neural network, GRU network and users' social network are used to model users, items, and social relations respectively. The experimental results on the datasets of Ciao and Epinions show that the recommendation performance of the proposed model is better.

articleTitle: Research on Logical Understanding of Video Surveillance Systems Based on Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Video surveillance systems are widely used in various fields, and enhancing the intelligence of video surveillance for better video understanding is a crucial topic. This paper conducts research on video logic understanding in surveillance systems using knowledge graphs and designs a video understanding system framework based on both prior and posterior knowledge graphs. The application system is developed using a Browser Server architecture. Finally, an experimental environment is set up in a 36 channel indoor duty scenario, resulting in a video understanding system with decision support capabilities.

articleTitle: A high-precision food image classification method with a small number of parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Image classification is a fundamental task in computer vision with diverse applications in various fields of life. In this paper, we design an improved convolutional neural network model for food image classification task. Firstly, a new feature extraction module DSC2f is designed to replace the feature extraction module of CSPDarkNet, to simplify the overall size of the model. Secondly, the Shuffle Attention module is reasonably introduced into the network structure, to improve the model’s ability to extract food-related features and enhance its overall performance. Experiments were carried out on the commonly used food datasets ETH-Food101 and Food2K. The top1-acc reached 77.31% on the ETH-Food101 dataset and 79.7% on the Food2K dataset. In the meantime, the proposed method reduces the number of parameters and calculations compared to other models.

articleTitle: Gated Graph Attention Recommendation based on Long- term and Short-term Preference
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The recommendation task based on the graph neural network model has made great progress in multimedia recommendation and social network recommendation. Compared with traditional collaborative filtering and matrix decomposition models, the graph-based social networks integrate the bipartite graph of user items and the user social graph. Use auxiliary information to further enhance the recommendation effect. Nevertheless, taking into account the efficient utilization of user’s preferences for social recommendations and the impact of local interdependent relationships among neighboring nodes; the dynamics and heterogeneity of the graph structure and other recommendation tasks, we propose a graph attention network that uses gated recurrent units model, fully considers the multiple user preferences. Apply a gated recurrent unit to extract user preferences. In addition, users’ long-term preferences change slowly, and we use specific vectors to represent embedded long-term features. By comparing multiple baselines on two datasets, it can be concluded that our model is superior to the method compared.

articleTitle: PoissonNet: Single Image Detail Enhancement Based on Poisson Regression
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Conventional image detail enhancement approaches commonly rely on filter-based or learning-based methodologies. In contrast, this study introduces a novel frequency domain model named PoissonNet. PoissonNet comprises two fundamental components: a sampling network and a weighting network. The sampling network employs linear sampling techniques to generate sampling features of multiple orders, which have been empirically validated as effective constituents for capturing detailed characteristics. The weighting network plays a crucial role in generating weight matrices to facilitate the effective fusion of sampled features from different orders. In this research, Poisson sampling coefficients are employed to perform regression fitting on the sampled features of each order. The optimal solution, namely the detail layer of the image, is obtained by constraining the objective function through a logarithmic maximum likelihood equation. Extensive experimental evaluations substantiate the remarkable generalization capabilities of the proposed image detail enhancement model. Moreover, the model provides a visually pleasing experience when evaluated on internationally recognized texture datasets.

articleTitle: Road Traffic Accident Severity Prediction under Unbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, road traffic safety has been a major concern. Research on road traffic accidents is crucial to address people’s worries about their daily commutes. This study focuses on California, using U.S. traffic accident data from February 2016 to the end of 2021. The research employs two data equalization methods: single sample and mixed sample. Traffic accident severity prediction models are established based on the XGBoost algorithm. These models are compared using accuracy and ROC curves. The model with the "random undersampling + SMOTENC oversampling" sequence is the most effective. The SHAP interpretability method analyzes accident factors’ impact on the model results. Consequently, specific strategies for preventing road traffic accidents are proposed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hot Spots and Trends in Firefighting Research Based on the Statistical Method of CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to understand the research progress, research hot spots and research frontiers in the field of domestic urban fire protection, this article is based on 1128 documents included in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure database from 2000 to 2021, and uses Cite Space software to conduct bibliometric and statistical analysis. This study focuses on analyzing the distribution of research subjects and the status of cooperative relationships, summarizing the classification of research topics and the emergence of keywords, and exploring research priorities and development trends in the field. The results of the statistical method show that urban firefighting will be led by smart firefighting, with high-rise buildings, big data, artificial intelligence, and drones being important research directions in the future.

articleTitle: Application of Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method based on AHP in the Selection of Medical Air Compressor Types
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This paper adopts the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to decompose the indicators for the selection of medical air compressors, calculates the weights of each indicator according to its importance, and uses the Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method (FCEM) to select the type of air compressor that best fits the hospital conditions. The AHP and the FCEM are widely used and applicable, and they can quantitatively analyze many qualitative objectives and arrive at the optimal solution. This paper also demonstrates how to use YAANP software for AHP calculation and validate the results.

articleTitle: Method and application for estimating the density of broiler flocks based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the intensive poultry breeding process, precise regulation of environmental factors such as temperature and humidity is directly related to the breeding efficiency. Intelligent regulation methods are extremely important for cost reduction and efficiency improvement. The setting values of existing poultry house temperature and humidity controllers are mostly manually determined, which requires enormous labor costs. With the development of information technology, it is becoming easier to obtain breeding data. Starting from large-scale breeding data, using machine learning and other methods to intelligently estimate the optimal temperature and humidity of poultry houses is an effective way to solve the above problems. Considering that there is a strong correlation between temperature and humidity and the spatial distribution of poultry, this article starts with the density estimation of poultry groups, proposes a Transformer-based poultry density estimation method, and selects broilers as the research object. The results obtained from experiments on the broiler density estimation dataset (M2-fowl) demonstrate an average absolute error (MAE) of 20.97 and a mean squared error (MSE) of 33.15 for this method. These findings indicate the algorithm’s capability to provide accurate estimates of poultry density, establishing a groundwork for assessing the comfort levels in poultry houses and implementing intelligent adjustments to temperature and humidity.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Programmable Metasurface RCS Controlling Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Radar Cross Section (RCS) control based on programmable metasurfaces has significant research prospects in radar stealth and deception. However, traditional optimization algorithms cannot accomplish the metasurface encoding design for given RCS control indicators. Therefore, this paper proposes an RCS control inverse design encoding scheme based on a tandem neural network. The training set is based on a programmable metasurface composed of 1-bit polarization-insensitive metasurface units with good phase and amplitude characteristics in the wide frequency band of 7.87-12.44GHz. By combining forward prediction and inverse design in a tandem network architecture, real-time encoding design can be achieved. Simulation results show that by performing spatial encoding throughout the X-band, dynamic RCS control of the normally incident plane wave can be achieved, and the maximum RCS attenuation value of a single frequency point exceeds 20dB.

articleTitle: Automatic Extraction and Representation of Procedural Knowledge from Manuals
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Executing industrial activities require the assistance of relevant procedures, and it is necessary to automate such activities with well-organized procedures in the industry 4.0 era. Although some efforts have been made to understand easily obtained procedural text, how to identify and extract procedures from industrial documents still need to be addressed. Most of such procedures in industry fields have a hierarchical structure and are stored in unstructured documents, making the extraction a challenge. Therefore, we propose an automatic solution framework to extract irregular formatted and hierarchically structured procedures from unstructured documents. Our research contributions are three-fold. First, our study fills the research gap of automatic acquisition of procedures from unstructured document with the proposed method. Second, we created a generic knowledge graph schema for the first time to represent hierarchical procedures. Third, we quantitively verified our method's high accuracy and robustness in extracting procedures from multi-domain documents. As another unique contribution, we for the first time created a benchmark dataset and reported our method performance.

articleTitle: Ontology Modeling and Rule Execution Optimization in Smart Home Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The rapid development of IoT technology has led to the integration of smart home systems into people’s lives. The devices in the smart home system come from different manufacturers with different structures and functions, and there is a lack of linkage between the devices in the traditional system, and it takes a long time to execute the user’s commands. To solve this problem, firstly, a hub-based smart home ontology model is constructed to achieve efficient management of system devices. Secondly, the Ontology2Vec method is proposed to transform the rules and ontology model into a directed graph, and the graph correlation algorithm is used to find the relationship between the devices to better achieve the linkage of the devices. Finally, the system is validated through simulation experiments, and the results show that Ontology2Vec can significantly improve the rule execution efficiency of smart home systems.

articleTitle: Logistics Demand Forecasting Based on BP Neural Network Model Optimized by Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of logistics demand is an important method to reduce logistics operation costs and improve the efficiency of logistics operations. This paper establishes the logistics demand forecasting index system, replaces the logistics demand with the freight volume, analyzes the correlation between the freight volume and other indexes in the logistics demand forecasting index system, and forecasts and analyzes the logistics demand by using the BP neural network forecasting model and the BP neural network forecasting model optimized by the genetic algorithm, respectively. The study shows that the BP neural network prediction model optimized by genetic algorithm is more accurate than the BP neural network prediction model in predicting logistics demand.

articleTitle: Price Prediction Model Based on Multi-source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, as people's emphasis on healthy eating has increased, there has been a growing interest in asparagus. The market demand for asparagus has been steadily rising, leading to rapid growth in the asparagus industry. However, asparagus prices exhibit significant fluctuations, which have had a certain impact on the development of the asparagus industry. The price of asparagus is influenced by various factors, and its price fluctuations show clear nonlinear characteristics. Traditional forecasting methods have limited accuracy, and existing prediction models have failed to fully leverage the potential of multi-source information fusion to enhance prediction accuracy. To address the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes an attention-based CNN-LSTM prediction model. It utilizes principal component analysis to preprocess data from multiple information sources, extracting crucial factors that influence asparagus prices, and facilitates the fusion of data from various sources. Concurrently, LSTM and CNN-LSTM models are employed for prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that, in comparison to traditional forecasting methods, the attention-based CNN-LSTM model, which incorporates multi-source information, achieves higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of Comprehensive Water Quality Labeling Index Method in Water Quality Evaluation of Xiangjiang River
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Assessing water quality stands as a fundamental task in the holistic enhancement of the water environment. Only through precise and scientific evaluations can we formulate effective treatment plans and protective measures aimed at preserving water quality. The conventional singlefactor assessment employs the least favorable indicator among water quality parameters to gauge overall water quality. This approach fails to accurately portray the comprehensive water quality status and its improvements. Therefore, using the Xiangjiang River water quality monitoring data released by the Hunan Provincial Department of Ecology and Environment as the data source, four main indicators including DO, CODMn, NH3N and TP were selected, and the comprehensive water quality labeling index method was used to analyze the Hunan section of the Xiangjiang River. Water quality assessment was conducted on three water quality cross-sections in the upper, middle and lower reaches. The experimental results show that the comprehensive water quality labeling index method not only combines the advantages of the single-factor evaluation method and is capable of qualitative evaluation; it also overcomes the shortcomings of the evaluation method that only selects the worst water quality index as the comprehensive water quality category, which is not comprehensive and objective. It can perform quantitative analysis, reflect the improvement effect of water quality, and can be better suitable for water quality evaluation.

Author Keywords: Comprehensive Water Quality Labeling Index Method

articleTitle: Research on Automatic and Efficient Digital Image Recognition Technology for Citrus Pest Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: A convolutional neural network (CNN) expert system has been developed to address the significant challenges posed by pests and diseases on "Citrus King" navel oranges, which are highly demanded in both domestic and international markets. Traditional detection methods for these afflictions are slow, subjective, and costly, necessitating professional expertise. Utilizing artificial intelligence and digital image technology, our CNN is capable of intelligently analyzing real-time images of navel oranges. It can automatically and swiftly identify various types of pests and diseases, such as Huanglongbing, scab, anthracnose, and fruit cracking disease. This facilitates early prevention and reduces the incidence of pests and diseases in navel orange cultivation. Moreover, this method potentially eliminates or minimizes pesticide use, thereby lowering planting costs. Experimental results have shown that the CNN’s accuracy in identifying navel orange pests and diseases exceeds 90%, which is a significant improvement over traditional methods, and it also substantially reduces detection costs.

articleTitle: Research and development of quality problem case base under the background of industrial big data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to solve the dilemma of lack of quality data specification, low utilization rate of empirical knowledge and time-consuming and laborious analysis of processing quality problems in manufacturing enterprises under the background of industrial big data, a quality problem case base based on CBR technology was proposed. Firstly, the case base workflow based on CBR technology is designed. Secondly, the semantic structure is used to describe the important information in the history quality problem record and combine it into quality problem cases. Then, the nearest neighbor method and analytic hierarchy process are used to retrieve similar cases, and the case correction process is carried out with reference to association rules. Finally, the cycle of case base construction, new problem discovery, similar case acquisition, case base complement and perfection is realized, and an online case base management platform is developed.

articleTitle: A dense crowd tracking method using density map and optical flow
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Traffic statistics in crowded places can provide support for passenger flow diversion. However, dense crowd statistics has problems such as occlusion, small scale, and complex background. Therefore, in this study, a method is proposed to use density maps for head target detection and optical flow for target tracking. In order to reduce human missed detection or false detection, this study designed two tracking algorithms based on trajectory prediction and target feature modeling. The experiment compared the tracking performance of two methods in scenarios with overlapping crowds and the effectiveness of re-tracking after target loss. The results show that feature-based tracking method has better tracking results and can be applied to estimate the number of people in dense crowds.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Robot for Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low drug distribution efficiency and high labor costs in hospital, we design an intelligent medicine delivery robot (car). The robot uses MSP430F5529 produced by TI as the core controller; it dynamically identifies the ward number through the K210 camera module; it uses a photosensitive sensor to identify hospital path information; and it extracts motor encoder data. The rotational speed of the feedback motor is used as speed closed-loop information; the gyroscope angle sensor is used to assist the robot in differential steering for direction selection; ensuring the orderliness of the robot's operation. Finally, the MSP430 chip is used to process each sensor data and accurately control the robot in real time, so that the robot can intelligently identify environmental information and complete the drug delivery task quickly and orderly. Several simulated environment tests proved the solution works.

articleTitle: University Course Recommendation Based on Multi-source Educational Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In response to the course recommendation problem in the undergraduate teaching scenario of higher education, a recommendation algorithm based on a multi-source educational knowledge graph is proposed. Firstly, the course correlation is analyzed, and relevant data is extracted from various databases of the university for preprocessing. Then, a multi-path RNN encoding method is proposed to embed multi-source information into the educational knowledge graph. Subsequently, an MLP is utilized to model the interaction between students and courses, aiming to predict student course selections. Finally, a comparative experiment is conducted to validate the feasibility of the university recommendation method based on the multi-source educational knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Advancing Predictive Models: Unveiling LightGBM Machine Learning for Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Machine learning based models provide substantial improvements in capturing more complex relationships and trends. In this study, we employed a widely used machine learning algorithm called LightGBM. LightGBM is a decision tree based gradient enhancement framework that excels in nonlinear modeling. Compared to traditional methods, LightGBM can autonomously recognize features and discover deeper patterns and associations from massive data, ensuring high prediction accuracy and fast training time. In addition, it also has the ability to efficiently process high-dimensional data and large-scale datasets, ensuring prediction accuracy and training efficiency. By using the LightGBM algorithm, we aim to improve the accuracy, reliability, and interpretability of predictions, providing investors with more comprehensive and accurate information.

articleTitle: An Influence Spread Blocking Maximization Method based on Node Mixed Blocking Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: While online social networks make it easier for people to share information, they can also accelerate the spread of unwanted information, which can have a serious impact on society. Therefore, this paper investigates the problem of influence spread blocking maximization, and introduces the concept of mixed blocking gain of nodes, i.e. the ability of nodes to blocking influence spread can be measured by the node’s activation probability and the influence probability propagated to other nodes, and based on this, the mixed blocking gain of the node is estimated. And a heuristic greedy algorithm is designed to select the node with the maximum blocking gain in each iteration and add it to the set of blocking nodes. Finally, it is compared with commonly used algorithms on real social network datasets of different sizes, and the results indicate that the algorithm in this paper has better influence spread blocking and can be applied to large-scale networks.

articleTitle: Fluid Inclusion Detection Based on Improved YOLOX
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Fluid inclusions, which are minuscule cavities within minerals or rocks that contain trapped fluids, have significant implications in various scientific and industrial fields. Detecting these inclusions presents a unique challenge, especially when dealing with numerous small to medium-sized targets in densely packed photomicrographs. These conditions often lead to challenges in feature extraction and lower detection accuracy. To address this, our study introduces a refined fluid inclusion detection methodology leveraging the enhanced YOLOX algorithm. We utilize a sliding window technique to segment the photomicrograph, thereby improving the detection of smaller targets. Additionally, we have integrated the Convolutional Block Attention Module into the YOLOX algorithm’s Neck component. This integration enriches the feature representation by capturing both spatial and channel-wise attention, which significantly boosts localization accuracy. Furthermore, we have adopted the Smooth Intersection over Union Loss as our loss function, optimizing the training process for both speed and precision. Our experimental results showcase that this improved YOLOX algorithm surpasses its predecessor, demonstrating an increase of 1.8% and 1.9% in AP50 and AP50:95 metrics, respectively. These empirical findings underscore the effectiveness of the improvement method in enhancing the precision of fluid inclusion detection.

articleTitle: BigChain: Consolidating Blockchain Client for Scalable Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Blockchains have been widely adopted to track critical data in complicated applications recently, thus it is necessary to provide efficient infrastructure to analyze large-scale chain data. However, the current blockchain clients are mostly designed for a single node with limited storage space and the separated data analysis systems are not suitable for huge chains due to redundant data transformation and scalability. To address these challenges, we propose BigChain, a distributed blockchain client with built-in bigdata processing capability. BigChain is designed on top of HBase by mapping blockchain entities to HBase’s KV storage to guarantee the rapid growth of on-chain data. By integrating the MapReduce framework, BigChain could leverage the Hadoop big data ecosystem directly to analyze blockchain data in a scalable manner. Additionally, an indexing service is devised accordingly to speed up BigChain. Finally, comprehensive experiments were conducted against Ethereum, and the results indicate that BigChain can outperform typical clients by 10 times in terms of comprehensive scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Social Recommendation with Global Dependency Modeling base on Self-Attention Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Social recommendation aims to provide personalized content recommendations by leveraging user relationships and interactions within a social network. It commonly employs techniques like collaborative filtering and graph neural networks. However, traditional graph neural networks often encounter limitations when dealing with social network data. They primarily rely on local information propagation and consider only immediate neighboring nodes, making it challenging to capture global dependencies comprehensively within the social network. In our research, we present a novel social recommendation model that extends the traditional graph neural network by incorporating self-attention mechanisms. This addition allows the model to better capture global dependencies between nodes. By considering relationships among all nodes in the graph, this module can identify long-range dependencies between nodes, providing more comprehensive information. This innovative model effectively enhances the performance of social recommendation, resulting in more personalized and relevant content recommendations for users.

articleTitle: Graph Structure Based Vehicle Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Predicting the path of motion is a critical element within the software suite that powers autonomous vehicles. Accurate foresight of surrounding traffic participants’ movements is essential for guaranteeing the proficiency and safety of intelligent driving. Artificial intelligence-driven trajectory prediction algorithms have garnered extensive research and implementation in recent times, yielding impressive outcomes. Nonetheless, sophisticated AI models are prone to uncertainty and lack transparency, potentially leading to unforeseen failures when deployed in real-world scenarios. The paper introduces an approach to trajectory forecasting that includes self-awareness features. The integration of an introspective element alongside a biphase training approach enhances the instantaneous efficacy of the existing trajectory prediction module. This guarantees that the system is prepared to tackle potential limitations in forecasting capabilities, a necessity for safe and dependable autonomous driving. Extensive testing and analysis have been carried out, and the methodology presented has shown strong performance in aspects such as self-awareness, minimal memory consumption, and prompt responsiveness, suggesting its potential as a resilient model for secure autonomous vehicle operations.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Federated Learning via Model Training
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The existing federated learning models have issues such as malicious central servers and malicious participants publishing false data to poison the model. Aiming at this case, this thesis proposed an improved decentralized federated learning model (IDFL), which moves the aggregation work from the central server to the local participants. In this paper, a proof-of-training consensus mechanism is proposed, which makes the election of block producers based on the quality of model training rather than the competition mechanism, thus effectively avoiding the block generation delay caused by the mining process, and also alleviating the blocking problem in the verification of model parameters in an asynchronous manner.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Hotspot Pattern Analysis of Air Travel Passengers with Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The surge in air travel and diverse transportation methods have intensified the challenges faced by airport landside traffic management. Conventional solutions, such as expanding terminal roadways, have become costly and inefficient in meeting the demands of intelligent traffic management. Leveraging the wealth of data, including GPS, deep learning algorithms offer a more effective approach to identify spatiotemporal patterns in air passenger travel and forecast hotspot areas. By proposing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based algorithm for predicting these hotspots and enhancing its accuracy through data fusion, this paper empowers airport authorities to proactively manage traffic congestion. The experiment showcases the algorithm’s superiority over baseline models, particularly in comparison to curve-fitting approaches. The combination of highly correlated heterogeneous data, like landside traffic flow and flight data, augments the accuracy of deep learning models. However, this predictive accuracy diminishes when data correlations are low. This methodology equips airport managers with insights into future traffic trends, serving as valuable reference data for future airport planning, thereby advancing airport management’s digital evolution.

articleTitle: A Differential Constrained Optimization Algorithm Based on Component Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The resolution and implementation of constrained optimization problems consistently remain a prominent subject in the realm of contemporary complex engineering applications. In this paper, the amalgamation of extraction and partitioning technology with the fundamental differential evolution algorithm is achieved, facilitating the transplantation of feasible component information through the algorithm’s inherent mutation operation and the segmentation technology’s feasible component breeding pool. Simultaneously, the adroit integration of adaptive constraint processing technology occurs within the original selection operation. In this paper, a component-based differential constraint algorithm is proposed and substantiated through numerical experiments conducted on common test functions. The experimental findings showcase the algorithm’s comparable or superior performance in terms of effectiveness, robustness, accuracy, and ease of implementation when compared to certain existing algorithms.

articleTitle: A Causal Inference Method Based on Front-Door Criterion and Difference in Differences for Analyzing Traffic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the period of pandemic, various regions implemented distinct control measures, leading to subtle changes in road traffic patterns. These fluctuations were further influenced by external factors such as public risk perception and weather conditions. Although prior research has employed observational methods to assess traffic states and applied causal inference techniques to passive data, the fusion of these approaches in the field of transportation remains relatively unexplored. This study endeavors to address this research gap by investigating the causal impact of pandemic containment policies on urban traffic in multiple cities across China. Our analytical framework combines the Additive Noise Model (ANM) algorithm with rigorous statistical tests designed to capture casual relationship. Specifically, we employ the front-door criterion and a difference-in-differences approach to validate these causal connections. Refutation tests and placebo tests are conducted. Ultimately, our methodology yields a generalized linear model optimized for predicting traffic patterns under varying intervention scenarios. Our research thus paves the way for incorporating causal inference methodologies into the formulation of resilient transportation strategies amid public health crises.

articleTitle: Overview of Marine Object Detection Based on Image
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Underwater object detection and recognition play a crucial role in marine scientific research and marine development. The optical features of underwater images are attenuated due to light scattering in the marine environment. Developing a model that satisfies the demands for detection precision and real-time performance while operating within the computational constraints of underwater robots poses a significant challenge. The intersection of progress in computing, underwater robotics, and artificial intelligence has garnered substantial scholarly attention in addressing this intricate issue. Underwater object recognition based on optical images or videos, under both artificial and natural lighting conditions, is aimed at achieving accurate detection and identification of submerged entities. This article succinctly delineates the procedural workflow for underwater object recognition, conducts a comprehensive scrutiny of cutting-edge algorithms, expounds upon the current research status and focal points in underwater recognition algorithmic research, and forecasts the prospective technological trajectory in this domain.

articleTitle: Robust Lane Detection with Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Due to the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, autonomous driving has recently achieved considerable progress. Lane detection belongs to the perception task which plays an important role of the subsequent task, e.g., planning and decision-making. It involves recognizing the boundaries of driving lanes and should be accurate and real-time. Existing approaches first locate the lane markings in the image and then post-processed it for navigation and safety. This research introduces an end-to-end lane detection approach that incorporates a knowledge distillation-oriented teaching module to forecast the position of the lane. With the help of polynomial regression branch, the teaching module guides the test one capturing the shape features to enhance the lane detection accuracy in challenging road conditions such as complex road layouts. Evaluations conducted on the CurveLanes, CULane, and TuSimple benchmark datasets indicate that our method outperforms the current cutting edge, demonstrating superior accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel CNN plus Transformer Network for EEG-based Automatic Sleep Staging
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Sleep is vital for human health, underpinning memory consolidation, restoration, and overall well-being. Accurately classifying sleep stages is crucial for diagnosing sleep disorders. Traditional sleep staging relies on experts reading spectrum analysis, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Current research methods are either multi-channel with high information dependency or single-channel but with low accuracy. Single-channel detection with high-accuracy results have been relatively lacking. Besides, most existing methods rely on hand-engineered features, which can be tedious and error-prone. In this paper, we propose a novel sleep stage classification system, named ConvTransSleepNet, which combines the strengths of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (ID-CNN) and Transformer layers. This hybrid architecture retains the inherent properties of traditional CNN models while incorporating the powerful self-attention mechanism of Transformer layers. The ID-CNN component is specifically designed to adapt to one-dimensional input data, such as biomedical signals like EEG. The transformer layers in ConvTransSleepNet allows the model to effectively capture complex temporal relationships and contextual information present in the EEG signals, further improving the sleep stage classification performance. Tested on the Sleep-EDF dataset, ConvTransSleepNet achieved an overall accuracy of 84.6%. Particularly, it demonstrated high accuracy for the wake, N2, N3, and REM stages. In comparison to other state-of-the-art approaches, our model showcased superior performance, with an overall accuracy of 0.84 and a macro-averaged Fl score of 0.79. These findings highlight ConvTransSleepNet's potential as an efficient tool for sleep stage classification.

articleTitle: Distributed cooperative jamming task allocation algorithm based on improved multi-pheromone ant colony algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of distributed cooperative jamming task allocation of UAV swarm, an optimal allocation method based on improving the cover efficiency of manned aircraft is proposed. Firstly, based on the cooperative interference of multiple UAVs, a model of common detection exposure area of networked radar is established.Then, according to the concept of safety zone in the jamming effectiveness evaluation criterion, a more objective and comprehensive jamming evaluation function model is established by combining the shortest distance between the manned aircraft and the exposed area boundary, the feasible area range for the manned aircraft to plan the safe track in the next step and the degree of suppression of the radar exposed area. Finally, based on the multi-pheromone ant colony algorithm, the adjustment and improvement are made to adjust the pheromone learning rate and path planning strategy more intelligently, improve the model optimization rate and optimization ability, and give the specific implementation logic. Through simulation, it is found that this method has more stable and fast convergence ability than traditional genetic algorithm, and has stronger global optimization ability than traditional ant colony algorithm. Especially With the expansion of operation scale, the convergence performance of the algorithm is more prominent, and it has better real-time operation and can be closer to practical application.

articleTitle: A real-time method for detecting Canada Goldenrod based on an improved YOLOv5 network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In order to improve the detection efficiency of Canada goldenrod, we propose an improved YOLOv5 network. Firstly, a channel attention module is added to the YOLOv5 network, which enhances target detection accuracy while maintaining the lightweight nature of the model. Secondly, a Spatial-to-Depth Convolution (SPD-Conv) layer has been integrated into the backbone network to enhance its capability to recognize low-resolution images and small targets. Finally, the substitution of the SiLU (Sigmoid Linear Unit) activation function in the initial network has been executed with a meta-Acon (Activate or Not) adaptive activation function. This adjustment serves to enhance the network’s generalization prowess and facilitates swifter convergence. Empirical findings indicate that the mean Average Precision (mAP) for the enhanced YOLOv5 network attains 65.5%, manifesting a 5.8% augmentation relative to the original configuration. The enhanced network leads to faster convergence and higher detection accuracy, better meeting the needs of invasive Canada goldenrod detection and control applications.

articleTitle: Tibetan Web Text Clustering Based on Contrast Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the field of natural language processing, text clustering, as a classical data analysis method, can be used to classify and analyze text well. This paper describes a novel clustering algorithm based on contrast learning, and carries out feature extraction, data enhancement and contrast clustering for Tibetan web hypertext data. This paper mainly introduces the data enhancement method based on pre-trained language model, and then uses contrast learning method to carry out deep clustering, and compares the traditional clustering algorithm. The feasibility of this method is proved by experimental evaluation. In the experiment, a variety of indicators are used to evaluate the algorithm, including clustering accuracy, normalized mutual information (NMI) and other indicators. The experimental results show that compared with traditional clustering algorithms, the proposed comparative clustering algorithm has improved in various indicators and has high accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This paper investigates the deep learning-based network intrusion detection model to address the problem of recognizing unknown attacks. By analyzing existing models, the potential of applying deep learning in network intrusion detection is explored, with a particular focus on the capabilities of discriminative variational autoencoders and generative adversarial networks in extracting and recognizing network traffic and attack features. We construct a deep learning-based network intrusion detection model with the aim of improving the recognition rate of new attacks and reducing false positives. By evaluating and comparing performance metrics, the advantages of the proposed model in recognizing unknown attacks are validated. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves higher recognition rates and accuracy for unknown attacks, outperforming traditional models in intrusion detection performance. This research provides important theoretical and practical guidance for the development and application of network intrusion detection.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Gastrointestinal Image Segmentation by U-Net Based on Ensemble of U-Net Models and Single Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: More than 1 million people worldwide are diagnosed with gastrointestinal cancer each year. About half of these patients are eligible for radiation therapy. Radiation oncologists strive to administer potent doses of radiation by directing beams of X-rays towards the tumor while ensuring the avoidance of the gastrointestinal tract and stomach [1]. The present objective is to direct X-ray beams towards malignant tumors while circumventing the gastrointestinal tract and stomach. This research presents a method for dividing the gastrointestinal organs (small the intestinal tract, the large intestinal tract, and stomach) into distinct sections. This technique aims to assist radiation oncologists in treating cancer patients with more speed and precision [1]. In this paper, the multi-path U-NET 2.5D model is assembled with U-NET 3D model for segmentation. In addition, among the proposed models, EfficientNet-B0 and EfficientNet-B5 are selected as the backbone models of U-Net to achieve high parameter and computational efficiency and more profound feature extraction capability. Finally, the Dice coefficient and Hausdorff distance are weighted into the evaluation index, where the Dice coefficient weighted 0.6, and the Hausdorff distance weighted 0.4. The final results show that the U-Net2.5D model (with EfficientNet-B5 as the backbone) has the best indicator when integrated with the U-Net3D model, reaching 0.8762. They are improved by 0.0244 compared to U-Net2.5D(EfficientNet-B5) alone.

articleTitle: HACE-Rec: Heterogeneous Graph Attention-based User-Content Interaction Feature Extraction and Personalized Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This paper proposes a content-side feature extraction and personalized recommendation method, which is based on heterogeneous graph attention model. First, the model will extract and convert the common attribute features of the content side into separate entity nodes, and perform graph modeling with the content nodes, and at the same time multi-type interaction between users and content is used to construct heterogeneous graphs to maximize the retention of information contained in the complex relationship between the user side and the content side; then, the heterogeneous graphs are used for feature mining and information analysis, which is based on the attention mechanism of graph neural network. Transmission and aggregation and update of node representation; then, fusion of information disseminated by each node on the user side and content side, calculation of matching score and integration of pairwise loss and graph loss to train the model and finally output the ranking of Top-K recommendation results. Finally, through comparative experiments with multiple benchmark models and ablation experiments on the loss function. Results show that the HACE-Rec model has improved the recall and accuracy.

articleTitle: A Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Method Based on Program Dependency Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The increasement of blockchain applications has brought about many security issues, with smart contract vulnerabilities causing significant financial losses. The majority of current smart contract vulnerability detection methods predominantly rely on static analysis of the source code and predefined expert rules. However, these approaches exhibit certain limitations, characterized by their restricted scalability and lower detection accuracy. Therefore in this paper, we use graph neural networks to perform smart contract vulnerability detection at the bytecode level, aiming to address the aforementioned issues. In particular, we propose a novel detection model. In order to acquire a comprehensive understanding of the dependencies among individual functions within a smart contract, we first construct a Program Dependency Graph(PDG) of functions, extract function-level features using graph neural networks, then augment function-level features using a self-attentive mechanism to learn the dependencies between functions, and finally aggregate function-level features for detecting the vulnerabilities. Our model possesses the capability to identify the subtle nuances in the interactions and interdependencies among different functions, consequently enhancing the precision of vulnerability detection. Experimental results show the performance of the method compared to existing smart contract vulnerability detection methods across multiple evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Mining top k best libraries in metaverse with random access and sequential access
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, the metaverse has gained significant attention as a virtual reality space where users can interact with each other and explore various virtual environments. As the popularity of the metaverse continues to rise, the need for efficient library querying algorithms becomes crucial. In this paper, we compare the top k best library querying algorithm with random access and sequential access with the linear querying algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed top k best library querying algorithm with random and sequential access outperforms the linear querying algorithm by being approximately 73.844% faster in range querying when k is 5. Furthermore, the relationship between the time consumption of the two querying algorithms and the value of k is discussed. The conditions where our proposed algorithm outperforms the baseline one are also indicated.

articleTitle: Automatic Registration of Mobile LiDAR Data and Multi-lens Combined Images using Image Initial Poses
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Even given the initial extrinsic of LiDAR and camera, high-precision automatic alignment between the Lidar scans and pictures acquired by mobile measurement systems (MMS) remains challenging due to clock asynchrony between sensors during data acquisition. In addition, the majority of images and mobile LiDAR Data registration methods are proposed for panoramic image sequences. A few research works have been focused on multi-lens combined images. We proposed an automated alignment approach for mobile lidar scans and multi-camera combined pictures using the initial poses of the images. First, we calibrate the extrinsic of the multi-lens combined camera and LiDAR sensor. Then, the odometry is obtained by the LiDAR SLAM algorithm, and the initial pose of each image is obtained. Then the sparse feature point cloud with the same scale as the lidar scan is obtained through the SfM algorithm with image initial poses. Finally, the iterative closest point (ICP) method is used to register the LiDAR scene points set with the image feature points set. The method is qualitatively and quantitatively evaluated on the indoor and outdoor data sets gathered from the self-developed mobile measurement platform. The alignment error of the approach suggested in this work is less than 1 pixel.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning Neural Networks in Sports Shoe Brand Classification Task
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has gained widespread attention and importance due to its outstanding performance in image feature learning. The rapid development of machine learning and deep learning has provided a powerful tool for handling complex classification problems and has achieved significant results. The development of neural network algorithms has also benefited from the progress in deep learning research. Deep learning is a machine learning method based on multi-layer neural network structures, which improves the modeling capability for complex data and tasks by increasing the depth and complexity of the network. For the task of classifying shoe brands, deep learning can help neural network models better understand features such as appearance, texture, and brand logos of shoes, as well as identify other everyday items to assist in their classification. After identifying the items, using different optimizers can improve the accuracy of classification, enabling more effective classification decisions.

articleTitle: Application of an Improved YOLOv7 Model in Disease and Pest Detection for Lychee Trees
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Disease and pest detection grounded in the principles of deep neural network architectures has become a prominent research direction in the field of agricultural technology, attracting widespread attention and emphasis from researchers globally in recent years. This paper investigates the application of an improved YOLOv7 algorithm in the detection of diseases and pests in lychee trees. It introduces a new Efficient Complete Intersection over Union (ECIoU) regression loss function, which, compared to the original CIoU loss function, enhances detection accuracy and convergence speed. By comparing with six other advanced models, the improved algorithm introduced in this manuscript exhibits superior performance compared to existing leading-edge models, in terms of mean average precision (mAP) curves, loss curves, and Precision-Recall curves. Finally, the improved model delineated in this document holds the potential to aid lychee growers in effectively managing pests and reducing the use of pesticides, providing practical benefits for sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Optimization Approach for Human Activity Using Smartphone Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: In the digital age, smartphones equipped with advanced sensors offer opportunities for predicting human activities. This paper presents a hybrid model, combining support vector machines (SVM) and random forests (RF), along with a soft voting classifier, to accurately predict various daily activities in real-time using smartphone inertial sensors. Our approach includes dataset acquisition, preprocessing, and feature extraction, demonstrating robust performance across different activities. The result section represents the performance of our hybrid model in comparison to benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Forecast of Wind Speed in Qingdao Port Based on Spatiotemporal Large Graph Network Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: This study presents a novel spatiotemporal graph modeling method for ultra-short-term wind speed forecasting in Qingdao Port. The proposed model, termed GWSTGM, is based on graph wavelet convolutional neural networks for spatiotemporal graph modeling and aims to improve the predictions of wind speed. The model effectively captures the spatiotemporal correlations of attribute features between nodes in a graph by incorporating a dynamic adjacency matrix for node embedding learning. Additionally, stacked dilated causal convolution is employed to capture the temporal correlations among graph nodes. The proposed model is evaluated using three distinct datasets, including traffic road network speed data and meteorological wind velocity data. The results demonstrate that the GWSTGM model outperforms other benchmark methods in short-term wind speed prediction tasks, highlighting its potential for uncovering spatiotemporal structures in input data. Future research will focus on the model’s performance in large graph structures and dynamic graph structures, as well as its applicability in various application fields.

articleTitle: A Survey About the Decision-making of Self-driving Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Self-driving mainly includes four parts: perception, planning, decision-making and control. The decision system is used to output safe and reasonable driving behaviors according to vehicle's state and surrounding environment, so as to autonomously control the vehicle to driving, which is the key part and core of self-driving. With the development of machine learning and AI, the self-driving technology gets further improvement. Using the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms to solve the behavior decision-making problems of self-driving vehicles has become one of the most concerned research hot spot. Traditional rule-based method lacks the ability to adapt the dynamic environments, DRL can overcome this drawback very well, it has unique advantage for processing those problems. In this paper, we summarize recent years research on DRL for decision making in the field of self-driving and provide a classification of driving tasks using these methods. And analyze in detail the advantages and disadvantages of DRL methods proposed by researchers for solving these driving tasks, and finally summarize some of the challenges and difficulties in applying DRL to complete decision-making problems and look forward to future research works and directions. The study contributes to a deeper understanding of the theories and methods related to DRL and decision-making of self-driving, and provides a reference for future research.

articleTitle: Clustering Analysis of Water Usage Structures Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: A key issue in the management of water resources in China is the adoption of a water supply total quantity control framework at the regional level based on socioeconomic development. This necessitates more effective management of water resource demand to achieve a balance between supply and demand. This paper aims to conduct an in-depth analysis of the industrial water usage structure, identify the primary influencing factors, and thereby provide insights for the design of demand management policies.
