Using a typical application scenario of "water extraction and supply" in a subsidiary of a water supply company in Beijing, a water knowledge graph incorporating multiple data sources is constructed. The study proposes a knowledge graph embedding model based on graph convolutional neural networks. Over the 36 months from 2019 to 2021, the water units in the accommodation, office, urban resident, healthcare, retail, education, catering, and residential services industries are clustered, and the water usage is analyzed. The results of this study are expected to provide references for optimizing urban water resource utilization.

articleTitle: Non-imaging Real-time Detection and Tracking of Fast-moving Objects Using a Single-pixel Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Detection and tracking of fast-moving objects have widespread utility in many fields. However, fulfilling this demand for fast and efficient detecting and tracking using image-based techniques is problematic, owing to the complex calculations and limited data processing capabilities. To tackle this problem, we propose an image-free method to achieve real-time detection and tracking of fast-moving objects. It employs the Hadamard pattern to illuminate the fast-moving object by a spatial light modulator, in which the resulting light signal is collected by a single-pixel detector. The single-pixel measurement values are directly used to reconstruct the position information without image reconstruction. Furthermore, a new sampling method is used to optimize the pattern projection way for achieving an ultra-low sampling rate. Compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our approach is not only capable of handling real-time detection and tracking, but also it has a small amount of calculation and high efficiency. We experimentally demonstrate that the proposed method, using a 22kHz digital micro-mirror device, can implement a 105fps frame rate at a 1.28% sampling rate when tracks. Our method breaks through the traditional tracking ways, which can implement the object real-time tracking without image reconstruction.

articleTitle: Research on Precipitation Catastrophe Based on Wavelet Permutation Entropy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Since the 20th century, Yunnan Province has been affected by drought throughout the year, causing huge losses to people’s production and life. To explore the coherence between precipitation and drought and the abrupt change characteristics of precipitation sequence. In this paper, we first use Morlet wavelet to decompose and reconstruct the annual average precipitation data in Yunnan Province to determine the significant period, and then use the daily precipitation wavelet real part under the significant period as a link to construct a complex wavelet network to determine the typical regions of precipitation change. Secondly, a wavelet permutation entropy algorithm is proposed based on the advantages of wavelet analysis in signal detail extraction and the mutation of permutation entropy to test the positioning accuracy. Finally, the abrupt change of precipitation in typical regions is studied based on the algorithm. The results show that the first and second significant periods of precipitation in Yunnan Province are 20 and 8 years, respectively. The typical regions of precipitation are Yuxi, Yuanmou, Huaping, and Lincang. The results showed that major mutations occurred in four typical regions in 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2011, and 2015, and severe drought occurred in each mutation. This verifies the validity and practicality of wavelet permutation entropy algorithm for precipitation mutation detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing passive target localization technology in UAV low frame-rate image sequences with a Joint Registration and Tracking module
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Low frame-rate image sequences, as an emerging visual information carrier, are favored for mobile platforms due to their low redundancy, storage, and transmission requirements. However, their poor spatial-temporal coherence poses challenges for visual tracking tasks, affecting the accuracy of passive target localization for unmanned aerial vehicles. This paper suggests a joint registration and tracking module to tackle this problem. The module incorporates a SIFT-based image registration submodule to enhance the accuracy of target prediction, thus improving the robustness of tracking and the localization accuracy of passive target localization technology. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s superior robustness in target tracking, achieving a target localization accuracy of approximately 4.5 meters at a flying height of 100 meters. Additionally, the data storage requirements are reduced by a factor of 29.3, significantly decreasing onboard computing and transmission resource demands. This approach provides crucial support for enhancing the accuracy and robustness of unmanned aerial vehicle target localization and is expected to yield substantial benefits in practical applications, playing a pivotal role in enhancing the capabilities and effectiveness of unmanned aerial vehicle missions.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Convolutional Neural Networks in Intelligent Editing for Short Video
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The emergence of short videos has led to the development of intelligent short video editing. This not only streamlines the intricate process of video editing but also empowers regular users to master editing skills. Intelligent editing, which relies on machine learning models and utilizes convolutional neural networks to process computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and other facets of editing, results in breakthrough achievements. Therefore, short video intelligent editing, which is based on convolutional neural network holds promising prospects and research value. This paper briefly describes the principle of convolutional neural network, introduces its application in clips, and discusses the defects of short video clips and research directions in future. At the same time, a scheme application of short video clip is designed to provide new practical ideas for research in this field.

articleTitle: BeOAC: Blockchain-enabled offline audit scheme in cross-chain interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: With the development of blockchain in recent years, it has found various applications in different fields. Nevertheless, the isolated nature and significant heterogeneity between different blockchains pose challenges for data exchange, impeding the progress of blockchain technology. To solve this issue, numerous cross-chain technologies are proposed. However, most of these cross-chain technologies concentrate on implementing cross-chain mechanisms, while neglecting the crucial aspect of ensuring data consistency during cross-chain interactions. Moreover, in scenarios with large data volumes and tight time constraints, existing cross-chain data consistency auditing schemes cannot complete the audit quickly. This leads to data users having to wait for a period of time to access the data. To address these problems, this paper proposes a blockchain-enabled offline audit scheme in cross-chain interaction(BeOAC) based on governing the chain by chain. The scheme uses non-interactive evidence generation and validation to support offline auditing, allowing users to quickly obtain the desired data. In addition, the scheme uses bilinear aggregation technology to enable batch auditing of data, improving cross-chain data auditing efficiency. Through theoretical and experimental analysis, it is proved that the scheme can verify the integrity of data in cross-chain interactions, achieving the functions of batch auditing. Besides, it protects the private data of users based on achieving secure and accurate cross-chain data sharing.

articleTitle: FraudNet: A Network-centric Method for Balancing and Detecting Anomalies in Healthcare Insurance
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Healthcare insurance fraud detection is challenged by the prevalence of class imbalance in transaction datasets, which undermines the accuracy of predictive models. Traditional data balancing methods have been insufficient in addressing the complexity of healthcare fraud. This study proposes a novel framework, FraudNET, which utilizes a hybrid of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Convolutional AutoEncoders (CAE) to generate a balanced dataset and enhance the detection of healthcare insurance fraud. The performance of FraudNET was evaluated against traditional models using metrics such as Precision, Recall, F1 score. FraudNET significantly improved the balance of the dataset, with the GAN generated synthetic data exhibiting high fidelity. The CAE model demonstrated superior performance in classifying fraudulent transactions, outperforming established methods like Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN) in comparative analyses. The integration of GANs and CAE in the FraudNET framework offers a promising solution to the challenge of class imbalance in healthcare insurance fraud detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotional Support Capabilities of Large Language Models through Cascaded Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Emotional support conversation aims to alleviate the emotional stress of the seeker and presents a challenging research task still in its nascent stage. It involves understanding the seeker’s emotional triggers and psychological intentions to provide suitable supportive responses. This can help mitigate negative feelings, especially when mental health resources are limited.While large language models like GPT have demonstrated powerful capabilities in areas such as writing, and long-text generation, aligning them for tasks in emotional support dialogue is problematic. These general-purpose models lack the logical reasoning and emotional comprehension required for complex human intentions, resulting in weaker emotional support capabilities.In this paper, we introduce a multi-model cascaded neural network system that combines dialogue state recognition, slot feature extraction, and generative language models. This framework enhances the emotional support capabilities of large language models by analyzing dialogue intentions and states, designing slots for different dialogue states, and extracting multi-dimensional information to guide the generative models. Our system utilizes non-deterministic finite state machines to model transitions between slot states, and we carefully design specific state transition functions to make the system more inclined to help users explore the deep-seated reasons for their emotions. The system can be configured to model existing psychological counseling and therapeutic methods, substantially improving the emotionally supportive text generated by large language models with only a minimal amount of training data.We evaluate the system’s capabilities in emotional support through multiple methods: automated assessments, human comparisons. Experimental results confirm that our system has a significant improvement in the ability of large language models to provide emotional support.

articleTitle: Automatic Knowledge Structuration of Automotive User Manual for Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Automotive user manuals serve as repositories of valuable information pertaining to a vehicle, leveraging question answering (QA) systems provides users with a convenient means to access this knowledge. In pursuit of developing an efficient QA system for such documents, this paper proposes the organization of the content into a structured knowledge graph-like triplet format.After conducting a comprehensive analysis of the automotive user manual content, we introduce a <subject, function, content> (<s, f, c>) triplet knowledge representation to represent the knowledge. Our approach involves a three-step pipeline for extracting these triplets from semi-structured XML documents. Central to this structure is the "content" node, forming the core of knowledge items. Leveraging the in-context learning abilities of an off-the-shelf Large Language Model (LLM), specifically ChatGPT, the "subject" and "function" components are induced from the "content" node. To ensure compactness and coherence in knowledge representation, a tailored phrase normalization process is designed to select identical phrases.Additionally, a LLM-powered evaluation method is employed to validate the extracted triplets, affirming their accuracy and relevance. This methodology demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed approach in automating the structuration of knowledge within automotive user manuals for seamless QA.

articleTitle: Time-delayed Geodemographic Scaling Algorithm for Fast COVID-19 Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Computer, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: COVID-19 has brought a series of challenges to human society and safety. Here a fine-grained COVID-19 Agent-based model (ABM) is proposed to investigate the possible outcomes of different policy interventions and their influence on subpopulations. A simulation platform is built to mimic the individual social contacts in different activities as the primary virus transmission way. Also, the simulation platform utilises a novel scale extension algorithm to enhance the simulation size while keeping the granularity, allowing the simulation size to range from a community with 30,000 residents to a megacity with 20 million residents. Finally, the model takes the recent Shenzhen outbreak as a case study to validate the simulation platform. The simulation results are consistent with the reported data, which lays the foundations to support different simulation scenarios to answer what-if questions efficiently.
